papers.title: On the Anderson Dual of $H\underline{\mathbb Z}$ and $H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we give complete classifications of the finite groups $G$ for which the constant Eilenberg--Mac Lane spectra $H\underline{\mathbb Z}$ and $H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ are Anderson self-dual up to a virtual representation shift, and we determine all such shifts. For both of these spectra, we determine the representation periodicity lattice for every finite group.
  As applications, we obtain $RO(G)$-graded universal coefficient theorems relating equivariant homology and cohomology, together with formulas for the Anderson duals of $H\underline{\mathbb Z}$-modules. In the $H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ self-dual cases, we identify the graded $\mathbb F_2$-linear dual of the coefficient ring $\pi_\star^G H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ with a representation shift of the ring as a module over itself. This gives perfect multiplication pairings and graded self-injectivity.

papers.title: Ramification in $\mathbf{E}_{n}$-algebras
papers.abstract: We study $\mathbf{E}_n$-algebras with ramification in their $\pi_0$ and in particular show that the existence of ramification places strong limitations on their chromatic behavior. In particular, we show that $\pi_0$ of nonzero $K(1)$-local $\mathbf{E}_4$-$\mathrm{KU}$-algebras cannot have a map from the ring of integers in a ramified extension of $\mathbf{Q}_p$, and we show that a $p$-complete $\mathbf{E}_2$-ring with a map from a perfectoid ring into its $\pi_0$ is an associative $\mathbf{Z}_p$-algebra.

papers.title: Elmendorf's Theorem for $\infty$-categories
papers.abstract: Motivated by Teleman's study of gauged topological quantum field theories, our main result is an analog of Elmendorf's theorem in the setting of simplicial group actions on $\infty$-categories. In particular, we prove that if $G$ is a simplicial group, there is a Quillen equivalence between the homotopy category of $\infty$-categories with $G$-action and the homotopy category of $\infty$-category-valued presheaves on the orbit category of $G$. We also show an analog of Whitehead's theorem in this setting.

papers.title: Higher Spherical Scissors Congruence II: Comodules
papers.abstract: We define the higher Dehn invariant on the Euclidean, hyperbolic, and spherical variants of scissors congruence $K$-theory, and prove that it makes these spectra into comodules over the spectral Sah algebra. This allows us to make the first formulation of the conjecture that the higher volume and Dehn invariants are jointly injective.

papers.title: Homological and homotopical epimorphisms in monoidal $\infty$-categories
papers.abstract: We compare homological and homotopical epimorphisms of associative algebras in monoidal $\infty$-categories. Assume that geometric realizations and pushouts of associative algebras exist and that tensoring preserves geometric realizations. Then every homological epimorphism is homotopical. If, in addition, the ambient category is additive and tensoring preserves finite coproducts, the converse holds. This extends the result of Chuang and Lazarev for dg-algebras. In the symmetric monoidal setting, we discuss consequences for centers and commutative refinements, as well as applications to derived analytic geometry.

papers.title: On derived equivalences of exact structures on the category of representations $k[x]/(x^n)$
papers.abstract: From the perspective of homological algebra, exact categories are interesting because they possess derived categories. Typically, an additive category admits many exact structures. If the original category is sufficiently nice (for example, quasi-abelian), a classification of exact structures can be given in terms of certain Serre subcategories in the category of contravariant functors. It turns out that the derived categories of different exact structures are functorially related. This work is concerned with sufficient conditions for the derived equivalence of different exact structures on certain categories.

papers.title: On Reed-Muller-Type Codes Associated to Proto-Exact Categories
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show how to associate a family of binary linear block codes to the class of admissibly cofinitary objects in any proto-exact category with rank function. This family naturally generalizes the well-studied family of binary Reed-Muller codes, and recovers this classical family for suitable choices of category. We also expand the list of known examples of proto-abelian categories to include incidence categories of posets. As an application of this result, we construct a binormal, combinatorial, proto-abelian category of Kashiwara crystals associated to any root system. In the case that the proto-exact category is a category of $\mathbb{F}_1$-representations of quivers, we show how to reconstruct our family via the language of algebraic geometry codes, in particular motivating an extension to arbitrary finite fields. We provide explicit computations of the dimension and minimum distance for select families of $\mathbb{F}_1$-representations of quivers.

papers.title: Semiadditive Power Operations in Chromatic Height $1$
papers.abstract: We recast the theory of power operations in chromatic height $1$ using higher semiadditivity. In particular, we show that if the height $1$ cyclotomic extension of a commutative algebra $R$ is Galois, then power operations on $R$-algebras are exactly $\delta$-ring operations. We also show that semiadditive power operations on chromatically localized algebraic $K$-theory agree with power operations defined using polynomial functoriality. As an application, we deduce that the map from the $K$-theory of a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear symmetric monoidal category to its $K(1)$-localization is a $\delta$-ring homomorphism on the level of underlying spaces. It is well known that operations on the $K$-theory of $\mathbb{Q}$-linear symmetric monoidal categories are $\lambda$-ring operations, and since $\delta$-rings are `$p$-typical' $\lambda$-rings, this is an instance of the redshift philosophy.

papers.title: Some chromatic height computations for homotopy fixed points of iterated topological Hochschild homology
papers.abstract: For an $\mathbb{E}_{\infty}$-ring spectrum $R$ of chromatic height $k$, the trace method and the chromatic redshift imply that $T^n$-fixed point of $n$-fold iterated topological Hochschild homology of $R$ has chromatic height at most $k+n$. In this paper, we compute these heights for $H\mathbb{F}_p$, $H\mathbb{Z}$ and the $p$-complete connective image-of-$J$ spectrum $j_p$ for all primes and $n\geq1$, which are exactly $n-1$, $n$ and $n+1$, respectively. Our method is based on properties of Wilson spaces and relative topological Hochschild homology over $\mathrm{MU}$.

papers.title: Spectra, Growth, and Localization in Half-Bounded Tensor Triangular Geometry
papers.abstract: Over a noetherian scheme, classical cohomological support determines thick tensor ideals of perfect complexes. In half-bounded derived categories, complexes with the same support can generate different radical thick tensor ideals. We study how these distinctions affect the Balmer spectrum and localization. For a commutative noetherian ring $R$, we prove that $\operatorname{Spc}(\mathbf D^-_{\mathrm{fg}}(R))$ is noetherian if and only if $R$ is artinian. For a nonempty noetherian scheme $X$, the corresponding condition is $\dim X=0$. For such a ring $R$ and a finite group $G$, $\operatorname{Spc}(\mathbf D^-_{\mathrm{fg}}(RG))$ is noetherian if and only if $R$ is artinian and $|G|$ is invertible in $R$. Using the Sanders--Zhang classification over a discrete valuation ring, we compare objects whose annihilator exponents grow at different rates in different degrees. We lift the relevant generation relations before changing coefficients and obtain spectral retractions. These comparisons persist after thick quotients and algebraic localization under explicit uniform annihilation and nonvanishing conditions. A second argument uses nonnilpotent classes of positive degree and passes from cyclic subgroups to finite groups. Applications include relative results for schemes and bounded-below spectra with degreewise finitely generated homotopy. We also describe the cohomological information shared by the resulting ideals. The localization comparisons for bounded-below complexes of finitely generated modules and for bounded-below derived objects with finitely generated cohomology are established separately.

papers.title: Stable homotopy theory of higher categories with adjoints
papers.abstract:
We demonstrate that higher categories with adjoints behave like homotopy types. By the homotopy hypothesis, homotopy types can be regarded as higher categories in which all cells are invertible. We show that replacing invertibility by the existence of higher adjoints still supports a homotopy theory that is at least as rich as classical homotopy theory.
  The basic invariants of this theory are the homotopy monoidal categories \[ \Pi_n(X,x)=\operatorname{Ho}\bigl(\Omega^n(X,x)\bigr) \] associated to a based $(\infty,\infty)$-category with adjoints $(X,x)$. These invariants are monoidal categories with duals and replace iterated loops with iterated endomorphisms. The classical homotopy groups of the classifying space are recovered as the isomorphism classes of objects in the groupoid completion. We prove a Whitehead theorem for homotopy monoidal categories and show that fibrations of higher categories give rise to long oriented exact sequences of homotopy monoidal categories.
  To develop homological algebra of higher categories with adjoints, we prove an equivalence between skeletal sequences of categorical spectra with adjoints and categorical chain complexes, extending a result outlined by Lurie in the proof of the cobordism hypothesis.

papers.title: The Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence can be arbitrarily non-degenerate in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: There is a long tradition of constructing smooth projective varieties in positive characteristic with non-degenerate Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequences. In this paper, we show that for any $n\geq 1$ and any spot $(i, j)$ on the $E_n$-page, except for the cases where the differential is forced to be zero for trivial reasons, there exists a smooth projective variety whose Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence has a non-zero differential with source $E_n^{i, j}$. Our construction is inspired by constructions of nilmanifolds in complex geometry and can be regarded as a positive characteristic analogue.

papers.title: Voevodsky's motives and zeroth slice of motivic sphere
papers.abstract: Let $S$ be a noetherian scheme of finite Krull dimension and let $R$ be a commutative ring in which every positive residue characteristic of $S$ is invertible. We prove that Voevodsky's stable Nisnevich category of motives with $R$-coefficients is canonically equivalent to modules over the zeroth slice of the motivic sphere with derived $R$-coefficients. The comparison identifies the corresponding commutative coefficient algebras and is compatible with arbitrary pullback. The theorem applies to singular and nonreduced schemes, including mixed-characteristic bases, and requires no excellence or finite-type hypothesis. Its special cases include rational coefficients over arbitrary bases, arbitrary coefficients over $\mathbb Q$-schemes, and $\mathbb Z[1/p]$-algebra coefficients over $\mathbb Z_{(p)}$-schemes. The proof establishes base change for finite-cycle spectra using permutation quotients, families of cycles, and arithmetic power homotopies, then passes to general bases by universal homeomorphism invariance and continuity.

papers.title: $RO(G)$-graded cohomology of a point is self-injective
papers.abstract: Generalizing known results for $G=C_2$ and constant $\underline{\mathbb{F}}_2$-coefficients, we show the $RO(G)$-graded Bredon cohomology of a point with constant $\underline{k}$-coefficients is self-injective whenever $G$ is a finite subgroup of $SO(3)$ and $k$ is a finite field. Self-injectivity holds more generally for the $RO(G)$-graded homotopy of the Eilenberg--MacLane spectrum associated to a $k$-linear commutative Green functor $M$, whenever the spectrum $HM$ is Anderson self-dual.

papers.title: Construction of holomorphic SCFTs with minimal index
papers.abstract: It has been an open question whether there exist holomorphic VOAs with N=1 supersymmetry and Witten index 1 for any positive central charge c. The existence of such a theory with c=288 is closely related to the 576-periodicity of the TMF spectrum via the Segal-Stolz-Teichner conjecture. Here we report the construction of thousands of such theories by extending the approach initiated by Gaiotto and Johnson-Freyd via ternary codes. In addition, for every positive integer k, we also construct holomorphic N=1 VOAs of central charge c=12k with index 24/gcd(24,k) -- conjectured to be the minimum -- in a computer-aided search carried out by AI coding agents. We overcome the exponential-time barrier by using chains of smaller cells to build ternary codes, whose indices can then be evaluated via a transfer-matrix technique, and we use a symmetric orbifold construction to reduce the problem of k=12 and 24 to that of k=6. Along the way, we also establish several results on ternary codes and their indices. Using an observation relating codes and Landau-Ginzburg orbifold models, we argue that the non-chiral doubles of the ternary code VOAs can always be gapped supersymmetrically.

papers.title: On explicit formulas for Grassmannian polylogarithms and Gelfand-MacPherson forms
papers.abstract: We answer a question of Goncharov by showing that his Grassmannian $n$-logarithm can be recovered by integrating the Borel invariant form on the symmetric space $\mathrm{SL}_{n}(\mathbf{C})/\mathrm{SU}(n)$ over a naturally defined ideal simplex. As corollaries, we recover the finiteness of primitive canonical integrals of Brown and the evaluation for wheel graphs of Brown and Schnetz. We also compute explicitly the Gelfand-MacPherson forms for powers of the first Pontryagin class and give a general integral formula for the Gelfand-MacPherson forms associated to each component of the Pontryagin character.

papers.title: On the enriched approximate completeness
papers.abstract:
We generalize to the enriched setting the classical theorem of Freyd, that the free cocompletion ${\mathscr PA}$ of a category ${\mathscr A}$ is complete if and only if ${\mathscr A}$ is approximately complete.
  The work of Day and Lack, arXiv:math/0610439, has laid the foundations for such a generalization and has had multiple applications in homotopy theory and in category theory. Our result allows us to expand on some of these applications.

papers.title: The flipping principle for boundedly acyclic covers and colorings
papers.abstract: Based on the theory of multicomplexes and other ideas by Gromov, we describe the flipping principle. This is an easy geometric criterion that forces the vanishing of the Gromov norm of homology classes. We use it to provide proofs based on a common geometric principle of the Vanishing Theorem and the Amenable Reduction Lemma by Gromov in the case of amenable and boundedly acyclic covers and colorings. We also strengthen the conclusion of the Amenable Reduction Lemma by showing that it implies the $\ell^1$-invisibility of the homology classes and not only the vanishing of their Gromov norm.

papers.title: A cohomology operation encoding the octahedral axiom
papers.abstract: We introduce a new secondary cohomology operation, the naturality defect product, associated with a graded natural transformation between the cohomology functors of two differential graded functors, and study its main properties. We then prove that a pretriangulated category satisfies the octahedral axiom if and only if the naturality defect product associated with the natural isomorphism given by a theorem of Heller vanishes on the homotopy category of acyclic complexes over it. This characterization extends immediately to n-angulated categories. As an application, we exhibit non-vanishing instances for the recently found examples of pretriangulated categories which are not triangulated. Finally, we show that horizontal composition of these natural isomorphisms preserves n-angulated structures, and we use it to obtain, from each of these examples and for every r >= 1, a pre-3r-angulated category which is not 3r-angulated.

papers.title: Derived products and completion defects of inverse limits
papers.abstract: We compute derived products and inverse limits in Grothendieck categories by exact coresolutions. For the product of $r$ doubled affine lines over $B[s]$, where $B$ is any nonzero commutative ring,the exact dimensions of products, epimorphic countable limits, and arbitrary countable limits are $r$, $r$, and $r+1$. We identify the top derived functors for every $B$-module of coefficients. Both obstruction modules contain the countable reduced product as a natural $B$-module direct summand, and a formal-series map relates them by an explicit cokernel sequence. A relative cofree coresolution gives degree shifts over an arbitrary Grothendieck category and computes the localization defect for arbitrary locally nilpotent diagrams. We also construct transfinite scalar extensions preserving a prescribed kernel and its derived limit;these give nonzero completion defects beyond any fixed ordinal.The general epimorphic top-degree vanishing question is not settled by these constructions.

papers.title: Quantitative $K$-homology of uniform Roe algebras
papers.abstract: We introduce quantitative $K$-homology for uniform Roe algebras of discrete proper metric spaces with bounded geometry, based on the controlled $KK$-theory of Willett and Yu. We construct a comparison map from Lipschitz $K$-theory and prove that, for chain geodesic spaces, it is an isomorphism in a quantitative sense; in particular, quantitative $K$-homology is isomorphic to the inverse limit of the Lipschitz $K$-theory groups as the Lipschitz constant tends to zero. We also establish a pairing between quantitative $K$-homology and quantitative $K$-theory.

papers.title: 2-Segal sets and pseudomonoids in the bicategory of spans
papers.abstract:
In this survey article, we give an introduction to the notion of a 2-Segal set and prove that 2-Segal sets are equivalent to pseudomonoids in the bicategory of spans. The proof utilizes graphical techniques for 2-Segal sets and spans that should be useful in more general settings.
  There are procedures for obtaining an associative algebra from a 2-Segal set (satisfying finiteness conditions). We describe these procedures and give several examples of algebras arising from 2-Segal sets.
  Wherever possible, we avoid higher category theory so as to make the paper accessible to a wide audience.

papers.title: A $2^{o(n)}$ Time Algorithm for 3-SAT
papers.abstract: We refute the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH) by presenting a deterministic algorithm for 3-SAT on n variables that runs in $2^{o(n)}$ time. Our algorithm in fact solves the harder problem #3-SAT, providing a count of the number of satisfying assignments. The result was discovered by an internal research Claude model and has been formalized in Lean 4.

papers.title: A categorical formulation of Kraus' paradox
papers.abstract: We give a categorical formulation of Kraus' "magic trick" for recovering information from truncated types. Rather than type theory, we work in Van den Berg-Moerdijk path categories with a univalent universe, and rather than propositional truncation we work with arbitrary cofibrations, which includes truncation as a special case. We show, using Kraus' argument that any cofibration with homogeneous domain is a monomorphism. We give some simple concrete examples in groupoids to illustrate the interaction between homogeneous types, cofibrations and univalent fibrations.

papers.title: A continuum whose hyperspace of regular subcontinua is homeomorphic to the irrationals
papers.abstract: For a metric continuum $X$, let $D(X)$ be the hyperspace of subcontinua of $X$ equal to the closure of their interior, with the Hausdorff metric. Camargo, Ordo\~nez and Ram\'irez asked whether $D(X)$ can be homeomorphic to the rationals or to the irrationals. We answer the latter question affirmatively. We construct a continuum $X\subseteq\ell^2$ as the closure of a countable tree of scaled copies of an indecomposable plane continuum. Two types of piece alternate: blocks with dense interior, and spines with empty interior carrying densely attached blocks. We characterize all regular subcontinua by nonempty convex sets of pieces satisfying a density condition, and prove that this coding is a homeomorphism onto a $G_\delta$ subset of a Cantor cube. We then show that no point of $D(X)$ has a compact neighborhood. The Alexandrov--Urysohn characterization yields $D(X)\cong\N^\N$, and hence $D(X)$ is homeomorphic to the irrationals. We also explain why this construction does not extend to the rational case, which remains open. Github repository: https://github.com/LucasAlves8Sp/A-CONTINUUM-WHOSE-HYPERSPACE-OF-REGULAR-SUBCONTINUA-IS-HOMEOMORPHIC-TO-THE-IRRATIONALS

papers.title: A geometric construction of supercuspidal representations
papers.abstract: We extend the framework of deep level Deligne-Lusztig varieties to the case of arbitrary residue characteristics $p > 0$. As an application, we provide a construction of a large class of (new) supercuspidal representations for unramified $p$-adic groups with arbitrary residue fields, in a purely geometric way.

papers.title: A lower explicit threshold for Chen's theorem under GRH
papers.abstract: Assume the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH). We show that every even integer $N \ge \exp(\exp(13.375))$ can be written as $N = p + P_2$, where $p$ is a prime and $P_2$ is either a prime or a product of two primes. The result is conditional on GRH and on Theorems 5, 6, 7 and Lemma 9 of Bordignon and Starichkova, Ramanujan J. 64 (2024), together with the auxiliary lemmas, Table 1 and display (6) that their Section 5.4 uses, at new parameter values; they obtain $\exp(\exp(14))$. It is not a new method: it is a re-choice of the parameters $u$ and $\alpha$ in their argument, combined with the observation that Chen's theorem needs only that the Section 5.4 main-term combination be positive, not that it exceed $4\cdot 10^{-3}$, because the inequality $\pi_2'(N) \ge \pi_2(N) - \sqrt{N} - 1$ from the proof of their Corollary 1 gives $N = p + P_2$ as soon as $\pi_2(N) > \sqrt{N} + 1$. The arithmetic of Section 5.4 at the new parameters and the parameter range inequalities are verified unconditionally in Lean 4.

papers.title: A nonstandard selfinjective algebra of Euclidean type
papers.abstract: Let $\Bbbk$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from $2$. We realize the four-dimensional selfinjective algebra $\Omega(1)$ as an admissible infinite cyclic orbit algebra of the repetitive Kronecker category. Thus an algebra long stated to be nonstandard is of Euclidean type in the orbit-algebra sense. We also identify a gap in an earlier proof of its nonstandardness and give an independent proof by determining all connected Galois covering sources of $\Omega(1)$. Together, these results disprove the implication from Euclidean type to standardness in the equivalence explicitly stated by Bocian--Holm--Skowro\'nski (2004) and Bocian--Skowro\'nski (2005). They also contradict the standardness conclusion of the Proposition in \S2.1 of Skowro\'nski (1989); its main theorem in \S1.5 assumes standardness and is not contradicted by this example.

papers.title: A proof Gauss might have found
papers.abstract: Ben Green’s historical variant of Tao’s recent tenth discriminant challenge [5] asks how early Gauss’s class-number-one conjecture could have been proved using mathematics then in print. Through discussions with GPT-6 Astra and Opus 5.5, we construct a proof of Gauss’s class-number-one conjecture [1] from ingredients published by 1808, specializing the Frobenius determinant argument [6]. Counting values of the principal form and summing factorial valuations reduce the proof to a residue sieve below 17000.

papers.title: Airy limit for the Jack process and topological expansion
papers.abstract: For every $\beta>0$, we establish multi-time soft-edge moment convergence for a class of Jack processes, including the Jack--Plancherel process, a discrete $\beta$-analogue of Dyson Brownian motion. The limiting moments admit an absolutely convergent expansion in terms of nonnegative Brownian bridges decorated by pairs of equal and opposite jumps. At equal times, we identify this limit with the joint Laplace statistics of the Airy$_\beta$ process for $\beta\geq1$. The same Brownian expansion yields an asymptotic $\beta$-topological expansion of the marginal $b$-conjecture and, at $\beta=2$, an explicit nonnegative formula for the Witten--Kontsevich intersection numbers.

papers.title: Analogues of Traverso's Isogeny Conjecture for Some Unitary p-Divisible Groups
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be a prime and $\Bbbk$ an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$. Two invariants worthy of study for a $p$-divisible group $X$ over $\Bbbk$ are its isogeny cutoff $b_X$, which measures the amount of $p$-torsion necessary to determine the Newton polygon of $X$, and its minimal height $q_X$, which measures its distance to the closest minimal $p$-divisible group (in the sense of Oort). Traverso's Isogeny Conjecture predicts a bound on $b_X$ in terms of its height and dimension. The conjecture was proved in [NV07] and a refinement was given in [LNV13]; the latter also gives a bound on $q_X$. In this paper, we study these invariants when restricting to the class of supersingular unitary $p$-divisible groups $X$ of signature $(a,g-a)$, where $0 < a < g$, for $p > 2$, and prove further refinements on their bounds purely in terms of $a$. In particular, we provide a complete description of the possible values of $q_X$. Finally, we rephrase our results in the language of the $\mathrm{BT}_m$ stratifications of characteristic-$p$ fibers of Shimura varieties for $\mathrm{GU}(a, g-a)$ in the case of an inert prime $p > 2$.

papers.title: Asymptotic coefficients of Weil-Petersson volumes in the large genus
papers.abstract: Mirzakhani-Zograf proved the large genus asymptotic expansions of Weil-Petersson volumes and showed that the asymptotic coefficients are polynomials in $\mathbb Q[\pi^{-2},\pi^2]$. They also conjectured that these are actually polynomials in $\mathbb Q[\pi^{-2}]$. In this paper, we prove Mirzakhani-Zograf's conjecture.

papers.title: Automatic cocommutativity for the quantum-group comonad
papers.abstract:
We prove that the cofree Hopf algebra on a cocommutative bialgebra is again cocommutative, and in fact coincides with the latter's largest Hopf subalgebra. This answers a question of Ardizzoni-Menini-Saracco and provides a proof for a statement to the same effect in the literature, whose original justification contains an apparent gap. The result relies on (and is in fact equivalent to) the observation that cocommutative bialgebra quotients of arbitrary Hopf algebras are automatically Hopf. This latter statement strengthens the analogue due to Newman, which assumes cocommutativity for the Hopf domain.
  One application of the above is the following quantum-rigidity result for Hopf algebras acted upon by a covariant quantum group: an action by one Hopf algebra on another which preserves the unital-algebra structure and the comultiplication factors through an action by a cocommutative Hopf algebra which moreover preserves the entire Hopf structure.

papers.title: Automorphisms and Hodge isometries of surfaces with $K^2=p_g=1$
papers.abstract: Let $S$ be a minimal complex surface of general type with $K_S^2=p_g(S)=1$. By a theorem of Catanese, the canonical model of $S$ is a complete intersection of two sextics in $\mathbf{P}(1,2,2,3,3)$ whose equations admit a normal form, and the global Torelli theorem fails for these surfaces. We describe $\operatorname{Aut}(S)$ in terms of the coefficients of the normal form, prove that $|\operatorname{Aut}(S)|\leq 72$, and classify the surfaces attaining the bound: two surfaces with singular canonical model and a one-parameter family $X_r$ of smooth surfaces. For the surfaces $X_r$ we compute a basis of the primitive cohomology consisting of eigenvectors of a subgroup $\mathbf{Z}/6\mathbf{Z} \times \mathbf{Z}/6\mathbf{Z}$ of $\operatorname{Aut}(X_r)$, given by residues of explicit polynomials, together with the intersection form in this basis. We then show that the natural map from $\operatorname{Aut}(X_r)$ to the group of Hodge isometries of the primitive lattice modulo $\pm1$ is injective but has image of index at least $331\,776$, so that the Torelli principle for automorphisms fails for these surfaces.

papers.title: Automorphisms of $\mathbb{P}^1$-bundles over rational surfaces in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: We study $\mathbb{P}^1$-bundles over smooth projective rational surfaces over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, together with the actions of their neutral automorphism groups. After an equivariant square birational reduction to the projective plane or a Hirzebruch surface, we classify the possible induced actions on the base and identify the families relevant to relative maximality. For $p\geq 3$, we prove that every such $\mathbb{P}^1$-bundle is equivariantly square birational to one whose neutral automorphism group is relatively maximal, and we classify all bundles with this property. We also describe all equivariant square birational maps between these relatively maximal bundles and determine which are stiff or superstiff, the analogues of rigidity and superrigidity for $\mathbb{P}^1$-bundles.

papers.title: Bertini's theorem for $F$-rational $F$-pure singularities
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, and let $X\subseteq\mathbb{P}^n_k$ be a quasi-projective variety that is $F$-rational and $F$-pure. We prove that if $H \subseteq \mathbb{P}^n_k$ is a general hyperplane, then $X \cap H$ is also $F$-rational and $F$-pure. Of related but independent interest, we present a relationship between the characteristic and index of a $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein variety with isolated non-$F$-regular locus which is $F$-pure but not $F$-regular.

papers.title: Brauer--Manin obstruction for Weil restrictions
papers.abstract: For a quasi-projective variety $X$ defined over a number field $k$, let $X'$ be its Weil restriction with respect to a finite field extension $k/k'$. We prove that the Brauer--Manin set of $X$ agrees with the Brauer--Manin set of $X'$. We also prove the agreement for Brauer--Manin set of them given by $\mathrm{Br}_1$.

papers.title: Characterising canonical lifts of ordinary Calabi-Yau varieties
papers.abstract: We study Brantner-Taelman's canonical lifts of ordinary Calabi-Yau varieties and characterise their (quasi)canonical lifts in terms of rational $p$-adic Hodge theoretic data. We also show that these canonical lifts need not be of CM type and that the associated local Galois representations need not split as sums of twists of unramified representations, in contrast to classical results for abelian varieties and K3 surfaces.

papers.title: Characters of symmetric groups: sharp bounds on virtual degrees and the Witten zeta function
papers.abstract: We prove sharp bounds on the virtual degrees introduced by Larsen and Shalev. This leads to improved bounds on characters of symmetric groups. We then sharpen bounds of Liebeck and Shalev concerning the Witten zeta function. Our main application is a characterization of the fixed-point free conjugacy classes whose associated random walk mixes in 2 steps.

papers.title: Classifying Leibniz racks
papers.abstract: Lie quandles were defined by T. Fritz as a nonlinear generalization of Lie algebras, to serve as a nonlinear algebras of observables in generalized form of Hamiltonian mechanics. These objects were subsequently generalized in a prequel article to objects referred to as smooth Lie group families of smooth racks by the authors. In this article, we investigate a particular system of nonlinear functional differential equations whose solution in general provides a pathway to the classification of smooth Lie group families of smooth rack structures on any given smooth manifold. We then discuss a particularly practical ansatz for solving these equations, and use it to construct new families of examples, as well as prove a result on the sense in which the Bloch sphere is the unique Lie quandle structure on the sphere.

papers.title: Comparing Periodic Point Invariants for Parameterized Families of Maps
papers.abstract: We compare different periodic point invariants for families of maps parameterized over a compact manifold. Malkiewich and Ponto showed that, in the case of a single map, the Fuller trace is equivalent to the collection of Reidmeister traces of iterates. In this paper, we show that, in contrast to the case of a single map, the fiberwise Fuller trace is a strictly more sensitive invariant than the collection of fiberwise Reidemeister traces of iterates. This resolves a conjecture of Malkiewich and Ponto. We also prove that our construction gives a geometric representation of elements of the kernel of the ghost map out of topological restriction homology.

papers.title: Conjectures of Ashoke Sen: Scope, Exact Tests and Analytic Limits
papers.abstract: We examine thirty-six selected statements associated with Ashoke Sen's work on duality, tachyon condensation, black hole indices and string field theory. The purpose is to distinguish mathematical results within a specified framework, physical conjectures, and extensions beyond the assumptions used in a derivation. Exact product expansions reproduce known negative dyon indices in toroidal orbifolds; with the charge cone transcribed correctly, a finite scan contains thirty negative-index charge triples. These numbers concern the full index, whose sign need not agree with a horizon index after hair removal. For tachyon dust we give the characteristic flow, the corrected Hessian sign criterion, and precise hypotheses under which the first focusing time is attained. We also separate the D7 divisor on the F-theory base from its singular pullback to the orientifold cover and give a local weak-coupling family with an $I_0^*$ divisor. These calculations delimit claims; they do not disprove the homogeneous rolling solution or Sen's positivity argument under its stated assumptions. The accompanying formal certificates check specified finite computations and algebraic identities, rather than the catalogue's physical interpretations. Established results and later corrections are credited to their sources.

papers.title: Convex orders in root systems and quantum tangent spaces
papers.abstract: We classify the reduced decompositions of the longest element $w_0$ of the Weyl group of a semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ for which the corresponding Lusztig quantum root vectors span a quantum tangent space in $U_q(\mathfrak{g})$. We introduce a combinatorial condition on the convex order induced by a reduced decomposition, tangency, and prove that a reduced decomposition gives rise to a quantum tangent space if and only if it is tangent. The proof relies on a description of the coproduct of quantum root vectors in terms of the convex order, and on a projection in the right weak order attached to each positive root. Up to commutation, tangent reduced decompositions are obtained by concatenating the longest minimal coset representatives along a chain of cominuscule parabolic quotients; in particular there are none in types $E_8$, $F_4$ and $G_2$.

papers.title: Correlation inequalities for volume polynomials
papers.abstract: We establish sharp correlation inequalities for volume polynomials associated with covers of multisets. These inequalities simultaneously generalize the Khovanskii--Teissier and reverse Khovanskii--Teissier inequalities for intersections of nef divisor classes on projective varieties. They also hold for volume polynomials arising from convex bodies and Hermitian matrices, recovering and extending classical results such as the Alexandrov--Fenchel inequality for mixed volumes of convex bodies and the Hadamard--Fischer inequality for determinants of positive semidefinite matrices. As a combinatorial application, we prove a negative correlation inequality for partitions of bases of matroids that are linearly realizable over a field.

papers.title: Counterexamples to congruences in finite p-groups
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a conjugacy class of a finite $p$-group $G$. H\'ethelyi, K\"ulshammer and the author asked whether the number of conjugacy classes contained in $KK^{-1}$ is always congruent to $1$ modulo $p-1$, and whether, dually, the number of irreducible constituents of $\chi\overline{\chi}$ is congruent to $1$ modulo $p-1$ for every $\chi\in\mathrm{Irr}(G)$. We construct a group of order $7^7$ for which both congruences fail.

papers.title: Decomposition Theorem for Perfectoid Rings along General Ideals
papers.abstract: Using Andr\'e's lemma and the excision square for perfectoidization coming from $p$-complete arc descent, we prove new structural results about perfectoid rings and perfectoidization. The main result is a tameness theorem for torsion in perfectoid rings: if $R$ is a perfectoid ring and $I\subset R$ is an ideal, then the $I$-torsion in $R$ is $I_{\mathrm{perfd}}$-almost zero. This yields an excision-type decomposition of $R$ along its $I$-torsion part. We also study (semi)perfectoid rings and perfectoid ideals and take the opportunity to make some structural remarks about them.

papers.title: Deformations of Deligne's S_t
papers.abstract: Snyder and Spencer showed that every *ribbon* infinitesimal deformation of the trivalent category $\mathcal{S}_t$ underlying Deligne's $\mathrm{Rep}(S_t)$ comes from varying $t$. Here we remove the braided hypothesis: every pivotal deformation of $\mathcal{S}_t$, $t\neq0$, over a local Artinian $\mathbb{C}$-algebra comes from varying $t$. The pivotal hypothesis turns out to be automatic, so the same holds for monoidal deformations. Since $\mathcal{S}_t$ is not generated as a pivotal category by its trivalent vertex, the crossing must be added as a generator, and the Reidemeister moves only survive in a deformed form, with lower order terms in the $2$- through $6$-box spaces. An open condition on rotational eigenvalues lets us lift the crossing in a rotation invariant way. A handful of overlap computations, in the spirit of Liu's classification of Yang--Baxter relation planar algebras, then kill every lower order term up to a change of the chosen crossing.

papers.title: Deformations of the logarithmic tangent bundle of smooth projective surfaces
papers.abstract: We study fixed-determinant deformations of the logarithmic tangent bundle associated with a smooth irreducible divisor on a smooth complex projective surface. We derive numerical criteria for the existence of positive-dimensional deformation families. Using the Enriques--Kodaira classification and Miyaoka-type inequalities, we classify the minimal surface pairs whose logarithmic tangent bundle is infinitesimally rigid. We also prove monotonicity under compatible blow-ups and compute local comparison formulas for resolutions of low-multiplicity ordinary singularities of the boundary.

papers.title: Degree growth, orbit graphs, and functoriality for birational dynamical systems
papers.abstract: The purpose of this paper is to give a natural divisor-theoretic formulation of the counting method introduced by Halburd for computing degree growth, in a form applicable to birational dynamical systems on varieties of arbitrary dimension. Instead of counting only preimages of special values, we follow time-indexed divisorial conditions through singularity patterns. These conditions are recorded on normalized finite-window orbit graphs, where the relevant multiplicities are realized as divisorial valuations of pullbacks of time-indexed divisors. This construction explains how the elementary computations appearing in singularity patterns can be interpreted as degree relations on a single normal variety. We then show that further relations arise from the failure of functoriality of pullbacks: when the center of a divisor enters the relevant indeterminacy locus, a degree-drop divisor appears. Under suitable finite-type assumptions, the two kinds of relations lead to closed linear difference systems governing degree sequences. Several examples, including higher-dimensional ones, demonstrate that the two mechanisms are complementary and that their combination determines the degree growth in cases where either mechanism alone is insufficient.

papers.title: Delta Characters and Ranks of Minimal Subisocrystals of Abelian Schemes
papers.abstract:
Using the framework of delta characters on arithmetic jet spaces, we construct a canonical sequence of filtered isocrystals associated to an abelian scheme $A$ of relative dimension $g$ over a $p$-adically complete discrete valuation ring. These isocrystals map injectively via a canonical morphism into the first (rational) crystalline cohomology group $\mathbf{H}^1_{\mathrm{cris}}(A)$ of the abelian scheme $A$, directly generalizing a prior construction due to Borger and Saha. Pandit showed that the canonical morphism is a map of isocrystals. This then implies that the image of this canonical embedding coincides with the minimal subisocrystal $F_{\mathrm{cris}}(\Omega_A)$ containing the space of invariant differential forms $H^0(A,\Omega_A)$.
  Berthelot and Ogus showed that the dimension of $F_{\mathrm{cris}}(\Omega_A)$ is $g$ if and only if $A$ has an endomorphism that lifts the absolute Frobenius on the special fiber of $A$. As a primary application, for a general abelian scheme $A$, we show that the minimal subisocrystal $F_{\mathrm{cris}}(\Omega_A)$ can be viewed as a module obtained from primitive delta characters of $A$ via appropriate twists by the canonical Frobenius morphism $\phi$ induced from the theory of arithmetic jet spaces. As a consequence, we show that the rank of $F_{\mathrm{cris}}(\Omega_A)$ depends on numerical invariants arising from the theory of delta characters of $A$. More precisely, the dimension of $F_{\mathrm{cris}}(\Omega_A)$ is given by the sum of the exact orders of the primitive delta characters associated to the abelian scheme $A$.

papers.title: Duality theory for categorical theories
papers.abstract: We have generalised the notion of categorical theory in model theory to the context of coherent theories. We prove a duality result between the full sub-2-category of pretopoi which are categorical, and the 2-category of profinite monoids. We also study the geometry of profinite monoids via the classifying topos construction, and show it identifies them as a full sub-2-category of the 2-category of topoi.

papers.title: Dynamical Chowla conjecture for polynomials of several variables
papers.abstract: In 1965, Chowla conjectured that the mean value of the Liouville function at non-square one-variable polynomials is zero. This conjecture is a generalization of the prime number theorem (PNT). In 2022, Bergelson and Richter established a dynamical generalization of this form of the PNT. For non-square multivariate polynomials, one also expects that Chowla's conjecture is true. In this article, we extend Bergelson and Richter's result to multivariate polynomials whose Birch rank is sufficiently large in terms of their degree. We also establish analogous results for averages over integer points on algebraic varieties.

papers.title: Edge multiset dimension of subdivided complete graphs
papers.abstract: An edge of a graph can be identified by its distances to a suitable set of vertices. If the reports omit the names of these vertices, only a multiset of distances remains, and finding a suitable set becomes more difficult. We determine the asymptotic cost of this loss of information for subdivided complete graphs. Let \(K_n\) be the complete graph on \(n\ge3\) vertices, and let \(S_L(K_n)\) replace each edge with a path of \(L\) edges, where \(L\ge2\) is an integer. Let \(\operatorname{edim}_{\mathrm m}\) be the minimum number of vertices whose distance multisets distinguish all edges. For every fixed \(L\ge3\), we prove \( \operatorname{edim}_{\mathrm m}(S_L(K_n))=\Theta_L\!\left(n^{1+1/\lfloor L/2\rfloor}\right) \qquad(n\longrightarrow\infty). \) Retaining the names requires only \(\Theta(n)\) vertices. Without them, the cost is quadratic at length three, has order \(n^{3/2}\) at lengths four and five, and has smaller exponents at longer fixed lengths. We also settle existence at the two shortest lengths for every \(n\ge3\): no selection works at length two, whereas at length three at most \(\binom n2\) vertices suffice. The proofs combine a count of integer vectors with realizable vertex labels. Sidon sets distinguish endpoint pairs at odd lengths, and exact finite certificates complete the length-three construction.

papers.title: Elementary transformations of toric vector bundles
papers.abstract: We describe negative and positive elementary transformations of toric vector bundles in terms of Klyachko filtrations. We first determine the filtrations of the restriction of a toric vector bundle to an invariant prime divisor and then derive explicit formulas for the transformed bundle: only the filtration at the distinguished ray changes. As applications, we interpret adding and removing invariant boundary components of logarithmic tangent bundles as elementary transformations and recover the residue sequence for logarithmic cotangent bundles.

papers.title: Endoscopy for representations of disconnected reductive groups over finite fields
papers.abstract:
Let G be the group of rational points of a connected reductive group over a finite field. Based on work of Lusztig and Yun, we make the Jordan decomposition for irreducible G-representations canonical. It comes in the form of an equivalence between the category of G-representations with a fixed semisimple parameter s and a category of essentially unipotent representations of an endoscopic group of G, enriched with an equivariant structure with respect to the component group of the centralizer of s.
  Next we generalize these results, replacing the connected reductive group by a smooth group scheme with reductive neutral component. Again we establish canonical equivalences for both the rational and the geometric series of G-representations, in terms of essentially unipotent representations of endoscopic groups.

papers.title: Equidistribution of integers represented by standard quadratic form under arithmetic constraints
papers.abstract: We study the equidistribution of integers of the form $n= x_1^2 + \cdots + x_d^2$ under the arithmetic constraints given by $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^d$. The first step in addressing this problem is to construct modular forms whose Fourier expansion coefficients correspond to the counting problem over the quadric in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ induced by the standard quadratic form, subject to the aforementioned arithmetic constraints. The weak modular property of these modular forms allows us to use representation theory to identify the congruence subgroup to which our modular forms correspond. We then establish a necessary and sufficient condition for functions on $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^d$ that defines a cusp form. Finally, we conclude that the equidistribution phenomenon occurs locally on $p+1$ orbits for $d \geq 4$.

papers.title: Euclidean distance degree defect of singular projective varieties
papers.abstract: The unit Euclidean distance degree and the generic Euclidean distance degree are two well-studied invariants of projective varieties. These quantities measure the algebraic complexity of nearest-point problems on a variety, and in many examples arising in optimization, engineering, statistics, and data science, there is a significant gap between them. We refer to this difference as the defect of the Euclidean distance (ED) degree. In this paper, we provide a constructible enhancement and a topological formula for the defect of the ED degree of an arbitrary complex projective variety, extending our previous results from the smooth setting. Since the generic Euclidean distance degree is typically more tractable, our approach offers a new method for computing ED degrees in broad generality.

papers.title: Explicit equations of three pairs of fake projective planes
papers.abstract: We find explicit polynomial equations in their bicanonical embeddings into $\mathbb C\mathbb P^9$ for the pairs of fake projective planes labeled by $(C18,p=3,\{2\},D_3), (C18,p=3,\{2\},(dD)_3)$ and $(C18,p=3,\{2\},(d^2D)_3)$ in the Cartwright-Steger classification. We do this by starting with the equations of the commensurable fake projective plane labeled by $(C18,p=3,\{2I\})$ that were found in arXiv:2512.03213.

papers.title: Explicit Finite $p$-Group Counterexamples to the Amit--Ashurst Conjecture
papers.abstract: For every prime $p$, we construct a finite $p$-group $G$ of order $p^{498}$ and nilpotency class two for which the word $w=\prod_{j=1}^{12}[x_{2j-1},x_{2j}]$ admits a value $g\ne1$ whose fibre has size strictly less than $|G|^{23}$. This gives counterexamples to the Amit--Ashurst conjecture for every prime. We determine the exact fibre size by reducing the word equation to matrix equations over $\mathbb{F}_p$ and counting their solutions.

papers.title: Explicit Kodaira-Spencer maps over PEL Shimura varieties
papers.abstract: The goal of our work is to construct a class of morphisms between two canonical line bundles on integral models of PEL Shimura varieties via Kodaira--Spencer maps, and explicitly compute such morphisms and their effects on the canonical metrics of line bundles. This result provides a concrete method for comparing two canonical line bundles and the corresponding arithmetic intersection numbers. In particular, it allows us to give an explicit relationship between the height functions defined by these two line bundles.

papers.title: Exponentially large mu-coefficients
papers.abstract: Using webs, we prove that Kazhdan-Lusztig mu-coefficients for symmetric groups grow at least exponentially with the rank, already for pairs labeled by a three-row rectangle.

papers.title: Failing to keep the balance: explicit formulae and topological recursion for leaky Hurwitz numbers
papers.abstract: Recently a new family of enumerative invariants called leaky Hurwitz numbers was introduced by Cavalieri-Markwig-Ranganathan in the context of logarithmic intersection theory. They admit an interpretation via tropical covers where the balancing condition fails. We employ tropical geometry to prove a generalisation of the piecewise polynomiality of Accadia-Karev-Lewanski for leaky completed cycles Hurwitz numbers, and a different wall crossing that is cubic instead of quadratic. Using tropical combinatorics and generatingfunctionology, we also find closed formulae for one-part and two-part completed cycles leaky Hurwitz numbers in genus $0$. Working more generally with a view towards topological recursion, we use Hamiltonian flows to associate spectral curves to very general cut-and-join operators. Under mild analytic constraints, we find the appropriate spectral curves, and in case the leakiness is fixed, we show that the resulting enumerative invariants satisfy topological recursion. This provides a partial inverse to recent work of Alexandrov-Bychkov-Dunin-Barkowski-Kazarian-Shadrin producing differentials satisfying topological recursion for KP $\tau$-functions. In particular these results specialise to completed cycles leaky Hurwitz numbers.

papers.title: Faithful Localization of Vertex Algebra Modules
papers.abstract: We establish a Faithfulness Theorem for vertex algebra modules, showing that two complementary geometric localizations can jointly detect global algebraic structure. We apply this principle to vertex algebras obtained by BRST reduction from classical invariant theory and identify them, under natural geometric hypotheses, with global sections of sheaves of chiral differential operators. As consequences, we prove vanishing of BRST cohomology in nonzero degrees and simplicity, and show that every finitely strongly generated module is a finite direct sum of copies of the vacuum module. In particular, the corresponding module category is equivalent to the category of finite-dimensional vector spaces. For families associated with classical groups, we identify the associated varieties with Hamiltonian reductions, proving quasi-lisse-ness and the predicted identification with Higgs branches of the corresponding supersymmetric gauge theories. This provides geometric realizations of a broad class of vertex algebras arising from three- and four-dimensional quantum field theories.

papers.title: Fine points of the moduli space of cubic rational maps
papers.abstract: A rational point of the moduli space $\mathcal{M}_3$ of cubic rational maps is fine if its conjugacy class contains a map defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, and coarse otherwise. In the invariants $\xi_0,\dots,\xi_5$ that embed $\mathcal{M}_3$ in $\mathbb{P}(2,2,3,3,4,6)$, we prove that a point with trivial automorphism group is fine if and only if the quaternion algebra $(-m_{12},-2\xi_0)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ splits, where $m_{12}=\frac{1}{3}\xi_0^2\xi_1+\xi_0\xi_4-\xi_3^2$; we give the analogous criterion on the locus $\mathcal{L}_2$ of maps with an involution and show that all other strata are fine. The proof is constructive and yields an explicit descent. We prove that the obstruction class is unramified along every divisor of the compactification, that a prime $p\ge 5$ obstructs only if the point reduces modulo $p$ into the closure of one of the two codimension-two loci $\mathcal{L}_1$, $\mathcal{L}_2$ of maps with an involution, and that $\mathcal{M}_3$ has transverse $A_1$-singularities along both, above which the class ramifies; local densities predict that $\mathcal{L}_2$ is met modulo $p$ with probability $\asymp 1/p$, so that it carries the obstruction. A census of all 214,260,288 rational points of weighted moduli height at most 7 agrees with this mechanism and supports the conjecture that the proportion of fine points tends to zero like $(\log B)^{-1/2}$.

papers.title: Finite Directional Coefficient Modules over Euler Fibers of $A$-Hypergeometric Systems
papers.abstract: Let A be a d-by-n integer matrix of rank d, let beta belong to the d-dimensional complex vector space, and consider the A-hypergeometric system defined by the ideal H_A(beta), with relation lattice L equal to the integer kernel of A. No homogeneity, pointedness, or positivity assumption is imposed on A. We study directed formal logarithmic solutions simultaneously over all exponent lattices in the Euler fiber over beta, which form an uncountable family when L has positive rank. For a fixed L-generic direction, negative-support strata are described by rational sign polyhedra, and their directional boundedness is characterized by recession cones. On each exponent lattice, normalization reduces the infinitely indexed coefficient equations to a finite system of Euler, transit, and directional vanishing relations, represented by a finitely presented directional coefficient module. We prove that only finitely many exponent lattices contribute nonzero directed solution spaces and that every contributing coefficient module has finite length. Macaulay inverse-system duality then identifies the dimension of the all-lattice directed formal logarithmic solution space with the length of the all-lattice coefficient module. We also give an explicit formal-series realization and a polynomial colon-ideal criterion for all realizable lowest exponents.

papers.title: Finite Truncated Lattice-Length Data on Three-Dimensional Flat Tori
papers.abstract: We study what finite truncations of the lattice-length multiset can determine about a three-dimensional flat torus. For a full-rank lattice \Lambda \subset \mathbb{R}^3, let \lambda_1(\Lambda) \leq \lambda_2(\Lambda) \leq \lambda_3(\Lambda) be its successive minima, and let \mathcal{L}_T(\Lambda) record the lengths of all nonzero lattice vectors of norm at most T, counted with vector multiplicity. First, on the class defined by \lambda_1 = a and \lambda_2 > T, we prove an exact volume classification: the set of possible covolumes is (F(a,T), \infty), where F(a,T) = \frac{aT}{2}\sqrt{3T^2 - a^2}. The lower bound uses Oppenheim's classical determinant-minimization theorem for Minkowski-reduced ternary forms; an explicit perturbed basis proves every larger volume is attained. Second, we give a pair of positive-definite Gram matrices with equal diagonal entries and matching two-coordinate data but different determinants. This yields a quantitative obstruction to uniform finite identification and gives the lower bound \sqrt{3} for the worst-case identification-radius constant. Schiemann's finite theta-series determination theorem supplies the complementary upper bound \sqrt{7/2} after conversion from squared lengths to radii. We also record a cubic sign-product identity for the eight signed basis vectors and explain its limitations. All contributions are separated from classical inputs, and the possible optimality of the constant \sqrt{3} and the broader topological question are left open.

papers.title: Finiteness of algebraic Weil-Petersson totally geodesic curves in pointed moduli spaces
papers.abstract:
For every pair $(g,n)$ with $2g-2+n>0$, we prove that $\mathcal M_{g,n}$ contains only finitely many closed algebraic curves that are totally geodesic for the Weil-Petersson metric. We show that every such curve is an arithmetic quadratic Teichm\"uller curve and has equal heights for all marked maximal cylinders in every periodic direction. Although there are infinitely many arithmetic Teichm\"uller curves, we can bound the degree of the associated torus covering by the crucial equal-height property. This leads to the desired finiteness statement.
  We also prove that quadratic Teichm\"uller curves are characterized by the existence of a holomorphic splitting of the logarithmic cotangent Kodaira-Spencer map. This result is the analogue of M\"oller and Viehweg's characterization of Kobayashi geodesics in $\mathcal A_g$.

papers.title: From Cherednik algebras to knot homology via cuspidal D-modules
papers.abstract: We prove a rational generalization of Haiman's master formula, conjectured by Gorsky and Negu\c{t}: the bigraded Frobenius character of the associated graded of the finite-dimensional representation $L_{m/n}$ of the rational Cherednik algebra at slope $m/n$ can be expressed using the generator of the same slope in the elliptic Hall algebra acting on its polynomial representation. The filtration on $L_{m/n}$ is induced by the Hodge filtration on the cuspidal character $D$-module. As a corollary, we relate the triply-graded Khovanov-Rozansky homology of the torus knot to the sum of hook multiplicity spaces of $L_{m/n}$, proving a conjecture of Gorsky, Oblomkov, Rasmussen and Shende. We further provide a realization of the torus knot homology in terms of explicit coherent sheaves on Hilbert schemes of points in the plane.

papers.title: Functional van Lint-Seidel Relative and Gerzon Universal Bounds
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of functional equiangular lines in finite rank modules over subrings of $\mathbb{R}$. We show that van Lint-Seidel relative and Gerzon universal bounds hold for this most general lines.

papers.title: Geometry of holonomic modules over the first Weyl algebra
papers.abstract: We give a geometric description of the formal local data of holonomic modules over the first Weyl algebra, the algebra of differential operators in one variable. The exponential part of the associated formal meromorphic connection is encoded by a truncated jet of an affine plane curve at infinity, and the regular part by a regular formal meromorphic connection. We prove that these geometric data uniquely determine the `elementary' blocks in the formal decomposition of holonomic modules. The resulting correspondence is equivariant under automorphisms of the first Weyl algebra, including the Fourier transform.

papers.title: Gibbs Approximation from Coarse-Graining of Finite Systems
papers.abstract: Thermodynamic integrability in finite systems admits concave probability-response potentials beyond the canonical ensemble. We investigate how replacing an unresolved block of energy levels by its effective free energy constrains this class and determines the Gibbs distribution, both exactly and quantitatively. For a response family defined across all finite spectra, exact single-block replacement implies conditional independence within each block and selects the Gibbs family with its canonical free-energy normalization. On a bounded energy window, conditional log-odds discrepancies determine a common reference inverse-temperature scale and yield a dimension-independent total-variation bound. A discrete calibration protocol incorporates grid rounding, interpolation under stated regularity bounds, and finite-sample concentration guarantees. We bound the conditional log-odds discrepancies in terms of coarse-grained block-probability residuals through finite block suppression, a bounded outer-control displacement, and a local internal curvature bound. The estimate separates auxiliary system size, measurement precision, and probability conditioning. Smooth local perturbations show that finitely many observations do not uniquely determine the global response. Applications to finite-capacity reservoirs and fixed-coupling mean-force models distinguish work-form closure from temperature-energy scaling. For two subsystems sharing small, bounded, symmetric log-temperature fluctuations, the leading mutual information is half the squared log-temperature variance times the product of their reference canonical heat capacities.

papers.title: GKZ Systems and Gauss-Manin Connections of Families of Projective Hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: Periods of projective hypersurfaces satisfy GKZ hypergeometric systems, which may have solutions that do not arise as periods. For deformations of Fermat hypersurfaces, we describe the Gauss-Manin connection in terms of images of contiguity operators between GKZ systems. These images are also realized as Fourier transforms of minimal extensions of Kummer modules.

papers.title: Global invertibility of polynomial mappings and connectedness of preimages of large spheres
papers.abstract: We prove that a polynomial mapping $\mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ with nowhere zero Jacobian determinant is a global diffeomorphism provided the preimage of large circles are connected. In higher dimensions this result fails and we present families of counterexamples. Yet, in dimension $3$, we prove that if the preimages of large spheres are connected, then the Jelonek set of the mapping is not homeomorphic to a line and, provided that it has codimension at least $2$, cannot have a single end at infinity.

papers.title: Group-Frames for Banach Spaces
papers.abstract: In the literature, frames generated by unitary representations of groups (known as group-frames) have been studied only for Hilbert spaces. We conduct the first study of frames for Banach spaces generated by isometrically invertible representations of discrete groups on Banach spaces. These frames are characterized using left-regular and right-regular representations, Gram matrices, and group matrices on classical sequence spaces. A sufficiently large collection of functional-vector pairs using the double commutant of the representation is identified to generate group-frames for Banach spaces. Subsequently, we study Schauder frames generated by time-frequency shift operators on finite-dimensional Banach spaces. We derive the Moyal formula, the fundamental identity of Gabor analysis, the Wexler-Raz criterion, and the Ron-Shen duality in functional form.

papers.title: Handle decompositions and Kirby diagrams for the complement of plane algebraic curves
papers.abstract: The complement of plane algebraic curves are well studied from topological and algebro-geometric viewpoints. In this paper, we will describe the explicit handle decompositions and the Kirby diagrams for the complement of plane algebraic curves. The method is based on the notion of braid monodromy. We refined this technique to obtain handle decompositions and Kirby diagrams.

papers.title: Hartl's dictionary and a transcendence characterization of equicharacteristic local shtukas with complex multiplication
papers.abstract: We update Hartl's dictionary between $p$-adic Hodge theory and its equicharacteristic analog to include aspects related to the Hodge--Tate filtration in $p$-adic Hodge theory and its equicharacteristic analog, the Hodge--Tate--Taguchi filtration. Using this update, we establish a transcendence characterization of equicharacteristic local shtukas with abelian Tannakian structure group, matching a result of Howe--Klevdal in the $p$-adic setting. A special case of this result says that a formal Drinfeld module over an equicharacteristic local field has complex multiplication if and only if the Hodge--Tate--Taguchi filtration on its $z$-adic Tate module is algebraic.

papers.title: Height growth of rational self-maps
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a number field or a function field of a curve. Let $f$ be a dominant rational self-map of a normal projective variety $X$ of dimension $d$ over $K$, and let $h_H\geq1$ be an ample Weil height. Let $\lambda_1(f)$ denote the first dynamical degree of $f$. We show that there is a constant $C_{f,h_H}>0$ such that, for any $n\geq1$ and any point $P\in X(\overline{K})$ with well-defined forward orbit, $h_H(f^n(P))\leq C_{f,h_H}h_H(P)n^{2(d-1)}\lambda_1(f)^n$ if $\lambda_1(f)>1$, and $h_H(f^n(P))\leq C_{f,h_H}h_H(P)n^{2d}$ if $\lambda_1(f)=1$. Over number fields, the proof combines a new uniform upper bound for arithmetic degrees with a uniform comparison of point heights. Over function fields, it relies on the corresponding uniform upper bound for geometric degrees on a projective model.

papers.title: Higher-order Persistence Diagrams
papers.abstract: Persistent homology tracks when topological features appear and disappear across filtered data and represents the lifetime of each feature by a persistence interval. In multiple instance learning, when the instances in a bag use filtrations over the same ordered parameter space, we can compare relationships between persistence intervals across instances. No existing method is designed to aggregate collections of persistence diagrams in multiple instance learning into a single persistence diagram of implications between intervals. We introduce higher-order persistence diagrams to represent relationships between persistence intervals and recursively construct each higher-order persistence interval from a pair of lower-order persistence intervals. We then aggregate these relationships across the persistence diagrams in a bag. Explicit construction of this aggregate is computationally expensive, so we introduce harmonic aggregation to compute coordinates of the aggregate from the lower-order persistence diagrams without explicitly constructing it. Computing a harmonic aggregation coordinate has lower asymptotic computational complexity than explicitly constructing the aggregate. We evaluate harmonic aggregation against persistence landscapes, persistence images, and PersLay on random network model and real-world graph-classification benchmarks, and find that harmonic aggregation has the highest accuracy on the random network model benchmark and on most real-world data benchmarks. Source code is available at https://github.com/cfanning8/higher-order-PDs.

papers.title: Hilbert squares of genus 16 K3 surfaces
papers.abstract: We consider the geometry of a general polarized K3 surface $(S,h)$ of genus 16 and its Fourier-Mukai partner $(S',h')$. We prove that $S^{[2]}$ is isomorphic to the moduli space $M_{S'}(2,h',7)$ of stable sheaves with Mukai vector $(2,h',7)$ and describe the embeddings of the projectivization of the stable vector bundle of Mukai vector $(2,-h',8)$ over $S'$ into these two isomorphic hyper-K\"ahler fourfolds. Following the work of Fr\'ed\'eric Han \cite{Frederic}, we explicitly construct a 3-form $t_1\in \wedge^3 V_{10}^*$, such that $S^{[2]}$ is isomorphic to the Debarre-Voisin fourfold in $G(6,V_{10})$ associated to $t_1\in \wedge^3 V_{10}^*$. Then the reconstruction program is also explained from two perspectives, i.e. in terms of families of stable representations and families of twisted cubics.

papers.title: Hochschild theory of multiplicative sequences of algebras and coalgebra measurings
papers.abstract: We study coalgebra measurings between multiplicative sequences of algebras and the maps induced by them on Hochschild homology. The Hochschild theory of multiplicative sequences is introduced as a functor taking values in graded algebras in the symmetric monoidal category of chain complexes, constructed with the help of the shuffle product. We develop the universal measuring coalgebra, or Sweedler Hom for multiplicative sequences, as well as study several other Sweedler operations in this context. In particular, we obtain an enrichment of multiplicative sequences over cocommutative coalgebras. Using an appropriate theory of bimodules over multiplicative sequences, we study maps induced by comodule measurings on the Hochschild theory with coefficients, as well as the corresponding enriched categories. Finally, we consider measurings and generalized Sweedler operations between multiplicative sequences induced by comultiplicative sequences of coalgebras, and also the maps in Hochschild theory obtained from them.

papers.title: Hodge Theory and Grobner Degenerations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the behavior of mixed Hodge structures under square-free Grobner degenerations. We show that the weight-zero part of singular cohomology and the zeroth graded piece of the Hodge filtration are preserved under such degenerations, complementing the homological rigidity established in the seminal work of Conca and Varbaro. We use these results to settle their conjecture concerning the singularities of homogeneous coordinate rings admitting such degenerations.

papers.title: Hodge--Deligne polynomials and $S_n$-representations on the cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$
papers.abstract: We compute the Hodge-Deligne polynomials of the moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$ of stable $n$-pointed curves of genus two, together with the action of the symmetric group $S_n$ on their cohomology, for all $n$. Using Hassett's moduli spaces of weighted pointed curves, we first show that the generating function of the $S_n$-equivariant Hodge-Deligne polynomials of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$ is obtained from that of the moduli spaces of minimally weighted pointed curves by plethysm with the explicit symmetric function $Z=h_1-\sum_{k\ge3}(x+x^2+\dots+x^{k-2})h_k$; numerically, this is an explicit change of variables. The latter spaces map to $\overline{\mathcal M}_g$, and over each boundary stratum they are built from punctured universal curves and Losev-Manin spaces. Combining the stratification by stable graphs with Burnside's formula and twisted characteristics, we obtain in genus two a closed formula whose only non-elementary input is the cohomology of symplectic local systems on $\mathcal M_{1,1}$ and $\mathscr A_2$, known by work of Eichler-Shimura and Petersen. This determines the $S_n$-representations on all $H^{p,q}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n})$ for $n\le 19$ and on all even degree $H^{p,q}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n})$ for every $n$. We carry out the computation in all degrees for $n\le 18$, where it agrees with an independent computation by point counts, and in even degrees for $n\le 30$. As an application, we find that the even degree cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$ is of Hodge-Tate type if and only if $n\le 20$: the space $H^{23,1}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,21})$ is the multiplicity free $S_{21}$-representation with Frobenius characteristic $s_1\cdot h_2[e_{10}]$, of dimension $1939938$, so that $H^{24}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,21})$ is not spanned by algebraic cycle classes.

papers.title: Hodge-Deligne and Poincar\'e polynomials of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,n}$
papers.abstract: By studying wall crossings of Hassett moduli spaces of weighted pointed curves, we prove a recursive formula that reduces the computation of the cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$ to that of the moduli space $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,(0^+)^n}$ of stable pointed curves of minimal weights. For $g=1$, we further prove an explicit formula for the Hodge-Deligne and Poincar\'e polynomials of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,(0^+)^n}$. Combining these, we prove formulas that enable us to compute the cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,n}$ efficiently.

papers.title: How to get an attractive model
papers.abstract: We give a fourth-order Calabi-Yau differential operator, which seems to have been missed by earlier tabulations. We draw attention to this operator because of its clear geometric interpretation and evidence that it possesses a rank-two attractor, conjecturally giving a new example of a Calabi-Yau threefold with modularity properties analogous to those of an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$.

papers.title: Indeterminacy of period map and Griffiths heights for hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We prove that the period map $\overline {\mathcal P}$, from the GIT moduli space of degree $d$ hypersurface $X$ in $\mathbb P^n$ to the Baily-Borel compactification of the period image associated to the middle cohomology $H^{n-1}_{\rm prim}(X,\mathbb Z)$, extends regularly to $X$ if and only if $X$ has at worst nodal singularities (resp. suspensions of slc surface singularities) when $n$ is even (resp. $n$ is odd). This verifies and generalizes Laza-O'Grady's prediction on the indeterminacy locus of the period map for quartic K3s to arbitrary hypersurfaces. For Calabi-Yau hypersurfaces, we prove that the birational map from the GIT moduli space to the BBH compactification extends regularly to $X$ if and only if $X$ has semi-log canonical singularities. The results apply to distinguish the Baily-Borel and BBH compactifications. In the process, we answer two questions of Mordant on the Griffiths height for families of hypersurfaces over curves, which are crucial to the proofs of the main results.

papers.title: Integration in Hensel minimal fields
papers.abstract: We develop a framework of motivic integration in the style of Hrushovski--Kazhdan in arbitrary Hensel minimal fields of equicharacteristic zero. Hence our work generalizes that of Hrushovski--Kazhdan and Yin, but applies more broadly to discretely valued fields, almost real closed fields with analytic structure, pseudo-local fields, and coarsenings. In more detail, we obtain isomorphisms of Grothendieck rings of definable sets, with or without volume forms, in the valued field sort and in the leading term sort. Along the way we develop a theory of effective 1-h-minimal structures, where finite definable sets can be lifted from the leading term sort to the valued fields sort. We show that many natural examples of 1-h-minimal structures are effective, and develop dimension theory and a theory of differentiation in $\mathrm{RV}$ for effective structures.

papers.title: Intersection multiplicity of a sparse curve and a trinomial curve
papers.abstract: Let f $\in$ C[x, y] be a trinomial and let g $\in$ C[x, y] be a sparse polynomial with N monomials (N $\ge$ 1). We address the problem of bounding the local intersection multiplicity of the bivariate polynomial system f = g = 0 at an isolated root q $\in$ (C * )^ 2 only in terms of N . Our main result establishes that the local multiplicity of the system at any isolated solution q $\in$ (C * ) ^2 is at most (N -1)(N +2)/ 2 , independently of the degrees of f and g. Furthermore, we know that this bound is sharp for N = 3.

papers.title: Involution-equivariant topological recursion and mirror symmetry for the affine binary dihedral Calabi--Yau threefold
papers.abstract: We prove a closed-string remodeling statement for the affine binary dihedral Calabi--Yau orbifold threefold $\mathcal X=[\mathbb C^2/\Gamma]\times\mathbb C$, where $\Gamma$ is a binary dihedral subgroup of $SU(2)$. This target lies outside the toric setting of the Bouchard--Klemm--Mari\~{n}o--Pasquetti remodeling conjecture: the toric mirror curve is replaced by the type-$D_l$ relativistic Toda curve of Brini--Ma--Strachan, and the Chekhov--Eynard--Orantin topological recursion is replaced by the $\mathbb Z_2$-equivariant topological recursion of Giacchetto--Kramer--Lewa\'nski, run in the sign sector of the Toda-curve involution with the Prym kernel as its two-point input. We identify the equivariant orbifold quantum cohomology Frobenius manifold of $\mathcal X$ with the invariant Jacobian Frobenius structure of the Toda curve, and we prove that the B-model $R$-matrix, defined by regularized stationary phase, equals the A-side normalized canonical Givental--Teleman $R$-matrix on a chosen simply connected domain; this equality is anchored at the orbifold point through a semistable degeneration of the Toda curve. Comparing the resulting Givental--Teleman and Dunin-Barkowski--Orantin--Shadrin--Spitz graph sums then identifies, after a parity-twisted leaf substitution, the sign-sector recursion with the descendant Gromov--Witten generating functions of $\mathcal X$ in the stable range ($2g-2+n>0$ with $n>0$), and identifies the recursion free energies with the equivariant Gromov--Witten free energies of $\mathcal X$ for $g\geq2$. We also match the genus-one potential defined by the reduced calibrated tau function with the Gromov--Witten potential up to an additive constant.

papers.title: Isogenous components of Jacobian surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a genus 2 curve defined over a field $K$, $\mathrm{char}\, K = p \geq 0$, and $\mathrm{Jac}(\mathcal{X}, \iota)$ its Jacobian, where $\iota$ is the principal polarization of $\mathrm{Jac}(\mathcal{X})$ attached to $\mathcal{X}$. Assume that $\mathrm{Jac}(\mathcal{X})$ is geometrically $(n,n)$-reducible with $E_1$ and $E_2$ its elliptic components. When $K$ is a number field, we count such curves up to geometric isomorphism, among those admitting a model over $K$. For $n=2$ and $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{X}) \cong V_4$ we prove that, for each $N=2,3,5,7$, there are infinitely many curves $\mathcal{X}$ for which $E_1$ and $E_2$ are $N$-isogenous. For $n=2$ and $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{X}) \cong D_4$ the elliptic quotients from the two classes of nonhyperelliptic involutions are always $2$-isogenous, and for each $N=3,5,7$ only finitely many curves have them $N$-isogenous. For $n=3$ there are infinitely many curves with $N$-isogenous elliptic components for each $N=2,3,5$, while for $N=7$ there are only finitely many such curves with a model over $\mathbb{Q}$.
