Furthermore, we determine the Kummer and the Shioda-Inose surfaces for the above $\mathrm{Jac}(\mathcal{X})$ and show how such results in positive characteristic $p>2$ suggest nice applications in cryptography.

papers.title: Kodaira-type Vanishings via Non-abelian Hodge Theory
papers.abstract: In this paper, we use nonabelian Hodge theory to study Kodaira-type vanishings. In particular, we generalize Saito vanishing using mixed twistor $\sD$-modules. We also generalize it to a Kawamata-Viehweg type vanishing using $\Q$-divisors, and prove an effective global generation theorem, as an application. We also prove a relative vanishing for a projective morphism in the mixed twistor $\sD$-module setting.

papers.title: Les squelettes accessibles d'un espace de Berkovich
papers.abstract: We define a class of skeletons on Berkovich analytic spaces, which we call "accessible", which contains the standard skeleton of the n-dimensional torus for every n and is preserved by G-glueing, by taking the inverse image along a morphism of relative dimension zero, and by taking the direct image along a morphism whose restriction to the involved skeleton is topologically proper.

papers.title: Lie structures in homotopy and isotopy calculi
papers.abstract: We establish compatibility of Lie structures that appear in homotopy calculus of functors and isotopy calculus of embeddings. On one hand, we give a new proof of the Johnson--Arone--Mahowald result describing the layers of the Goodwillie tower of the identity functor, and we directly compare the spectral Lie bracket with the classical Whitehead bracket on spaces. On the other hand, we geometrically define a bracket on the layers of the embedding calculus tower for embeddings of arcs. These results are unified through the same technical tool, a newly defined bracket on total homotopy fibres of collapsing cubes of wedge sums.

papers.title: Lifting $\tau$-exceptional sequences
papers.abstract: We study the behaviour of $\tau$-exceptional sequences under passage from a finite-dimensional algebra $\Lambda$ to a factor algebra $\Lambda/I$. Assuming that $\Lambda$ is $\tau$-tilting finite and that $I\subseteq \operatorname{rad}\Lambda$, we construct, for every $r$ less than or equal to the number of simple $\Lambda$-modules, an injective map from the $\tau$-exceptional sequences of length $r$ over $\Lambda/I$ to those over $\Lambda$. The construction is recursive and is based on lifting indecomposable $\tau$-rigid modules and comparing their associated $\tau$-perpendicular categories. At each stage, we construct a right exact functor between the relevant $\tau$-perpendicular categories which, after identifying them with module categories, is naturally isomorphic to extension of scalars along a quotient $\Gamma\to\Gamma/J$, where $J\subseteq \operatorname{rad}\Gamma$. These functors send each lifted term to an object in the additive closure of the corresponding original term. Finally, we conjecture connections with known bijections for representations of quivers over local algebras and for Nakayama algebras.

papers.title: Line-filtered ACM bundles and Ulrich defects on abelian varieties of Picard rank one
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be a complex abelian variety with $\NS(A)=\Z[L]$, $L$ ample. We show that a vector bundle filtered by line bundles splits uniquely into unipotent blocks, determine when it is ACM with respect to $L$, and show that it is never Ulrich. For a rank-two Ulrich bundle we bound from below the degree of the defect of every saturated line subbundle, compute the Hilbert polynomial of the defect, and show that the bound is attained exactly when an explicit cohomological support locus is nonempty. On abelian surfaces this locus is an ample curve in $\Pic^0(A)$; as a consequence, every rank-two Ulrich bundle is a Serre extension of a fixed numerical type, which we characterize and construct for every ample $L$. For $g\ge3$, we reduce the equality case to the existence of subcanonical codimension-two subschemes with prescribed cohomology.

papers.title: Low Genus Curves on Compact Shimura Surfaces
papers.abstract: We investigate and compare the behaviors of complex curves on two major types of compact Shimura surfaces: compact variants of Picard and Hilbert modular surfaces. They are quotients of complex hyperbolic balls corresponding to moduli problems for abelian varieties with certain endomorphism types. We prove that if we fix a genus bound, then when the defining discriminant is large enough, low genus curves on the compact variant of Picard modular surfaces do not exist, while low genus curves may persist on the compact variant of Hilbert modular surfaces only if they are special curves, which parametrize those with extra endomorphisms. These results are special cases of a complex function field analogue of uniform boundedness on endomorphism types of abelian varieties. The proof requires understanding the repulsion of special subvarieties and relies on volume estimates in hyperbolic geometry.

papers.title: Matrix representations of ${\rm BC}_n$ associative Yang--Baxter equations and related long-range spin chains
papers.abstract: We construct a matrix representation of the algebra defined by the associative Yang--Baxter equations of ${\rm BC}_n$ type. In the elliptic case, two sets of generators are represented in terms of the Baxter--Belavin quantum $R$-matrix in the fundamental representation of ${\rm GL}_N$, while the remaining generators are represented by the elliptic $K$-matrix found by Komori and Hikami. We revisit its derivation using the Felder--Pasquier procedure and correct the unitarity relation for odd $N$. We then use these matrix representations to construct examples of long-range quantum spin chains from $R$-matrix-valued Lax pairs for the classical Calogero--Inozemtsev system associated with the ${\rm BC}_n$ root system. We also construct $R$-matrix-valued Lax pairs for Calogero--Moser models in an external field, leading to Haldane--Shastry and Polychronakos--Frahm chains with modified spin positions.

papers.title: Maximal curves with trivial automorphism group
papers.abstract:
We construct algebraic curves with trivial geometric automorphism group by taking cyclic scalar quotients of curves of the form \[
  y^r-y=xR(x),\qquad r=p^e. \] We give a condition on the genus under which the quotient has no nontrivial automorphism. The proof uses the ramification of a degree-$r$ morphism to the projective line, Castelnuovo--Severi, and explicit automorphisms of the covering curve. The quotient also has gonality $r$, with a unique morphism of degree $r$ to the projective line up to an automorphism of the latter. Applying the construction to maximal additive curves gives explicit maximal curves with trivial geometric automorphism group in every positive characteristic, including families defined over the prime field and of unbounded genus. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first examples of maximal curves with trivial geometric automorphism group. Every maximal curve in these families is covered by the Hermitian curve. For every odd prime $p$ and every $n\ge2$, we prove that the curve $\X_{p,n}$, maximal over $\F_{p^{4n+2}}$, is not a Galois subcover of the corresponding Hermitian curve, even over the algebraic closure. Thus every odd characteristic yields an infinite family of curves covered but not Galois covered by the Hermitian curve. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first such infinite families.

papers.title: Moduli Spaces of Homologically Trivial Parabolic (Higgs) Bundles on the Projective Line and an Application to the Deligne-Simpson Problem
papers.abstract: We establish an isomorphism between the moduli space of homologically trivial parabolic (Higgs) bundles on $\mathbb{P}^1$ and the quiver variety associated to a star-shaped quiver. As an application, we give a Hitchin-theoretic construction of irreducible solutions to the nilpotent additive Deligne-Simpson problem under explicit numerical assumptions.

papers.title: Movable Curves and Ample Normal Bundles
papers.abstract: We prove that the movable cone of a smooth complex projective variety is the closed cone generated by possibly singular curves with ample coherent normal sheaves, answering a question of Boucksom--Demailly--P\u{a}un--Peternell. For smooth curves, we establish the analogous equality in several geometric settings and give explicit constructions on blowups.

papers.title: Mustafin degenerations of six points in the projective plane and self-duality
papers.abstract: Mustafin varieties provide a framework for degenerating the projective plane together with marked points, governed by the combinatorics of Bruhat-Tits buildings. Such limit objects are parametrized by the boundary points of a projective compactification of the moduli space of $n$ points in $\mathbb{P}^2$ constructed by Schaffler-Tevelev. In this paper, we study the locus of this compactification generically parametrizing self-dual configurations, or equivalently, six points lying on a conic. We prove that this locus is a tropical compactification of the moduli space of self-dual configurations, with associated fan a refinement of the self-dual tropical Grassmannian introduced by Geiger-Hashimoto-Sturmfels-Vlad. We show that this compactification is a blow up of $\overline{\mathrm{M}}_{0,6}$ and we classify the objects it parametrizes: degenerations of $\mathbb{P}^2$ equipped with a stable $6$-pointed rational curve that records the limiting conic.

papers.title: New Bounds on Distributional Sectional Category and Applications to Distributional Homotopic Distance
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish several new bounds for the distributional sectional category ($\mathrm{dsecat}$). We first prove Jauhari's conjecture, thereby establishing a cohomological lower bound for $\mathrm{dsecat}$ with arbitrary coefficients. We then obtain an analogous lower bound with rational coefficients by constructing a natural graded $\mathbb{Q}$-linear section of the homomorphism induced in cohomology by the symmetric diagonal. As applications, we provide several computations of the distributional sectional category. We also establish multiplicative product and composition inequalities for $\mathrm{dsecat}$. Finally, we apply these results to distributional homotopic distance. A sequential version of this invariant was recently introduced by Jauhari and Oprea; we give an equivalent formulation in terms of distributed homotopies and derive new fibration and multiplicative triangle inequalities.

papers.title: Nijenhuis pre-Lie bialgebras, Nijenhuis Lie bialgebras and \sss-equation
papers.abstract: We develop a bialgebraic framework for Nijenhuis operators on pre-Lie algebras and coalgebras. Starting from dual triangular pre-Lie bialgebras and weak pseudo-Hessian structures, we construct Nijenhuis operators on pre-Lie algebras and establish the corresponding coalgebraic construction. We introduce Nijenhuis pre-Lie bialgebras, characterize them through matched pairs, and identify compatibility conditions linking the two constructions. For triangular structures, we formulate the $S$-Nijenhuis $\mathbb{S}$-equation, give an operator characterization, and obtain constructions using relative Rota-Baxter operators. We also show that balanced Nijenhuis pre-Lie bialgebras give rise to Nijenhuis Lie bialgebras. Finally, we introduce crossed modules and braided Nijenhuis pre-Lie bialgebras, and characterize when compatible algebraic and coalgebraic data assemble into a Nijenhuis pre-Lie biproduct. These results connect Nijenhuis operators with pre-Lie bialgebra structures, Yang-Baxter-type equations, and constructions on representations.

papers.title: Non-Induced Representations in Characteristic Zero
papers.abstract: This paper explores the failure of induction from all proper subgroups to generate the full representation ring, measured by a quotient group $Q_k(G)$. We extend existing results for cyclic groups to all finite abelian groups and calculate this quotient for all finite groups over fields of characteristic 0 by reducing to the abelian case. We briefly discuss extensions to positive characteristics via modular representation theory. Finally, we detail our result for certain well-known families of groups.

papers.title: Number of equations defining the Kummer varieties of hyperelliptic curves
papers.abstract: The Jacobian of an hyperelliptic curve $C$ of genus $g$ over $\mathbb{C}$ is equipped with a symmetric theta divisor $\Theta$ that defines a principal polarization. The line bundle $\mathcal{O}(2\Theta)$ defines an embedding of the Kummer variety $K$ inside the projective space $\mathbb{P}^{2^g-1}$, which factorizes inside a certain orthogonal Grassmannian. We describe a minimal free resolution of $K$ inside this Grassmannian using geometric representation theory. As a consequence, we obtain a formula for the number of quartic equations defining $K$ in the projective space $\mathbb{P}^{2^g-1}$.

papers.title: Number of left cells in the second lowest two-sided cell
papers.abstract: We prove Shi's conjecture that the number of left cells in the second lowest two-sided cell of the affine Weyl group attached to a simply connected simple complex group $G$ is exactly $|W_0|/2$, where $W_0$ is the corresponding finite Weyl group. The same formula holds for the corresponding extended affine Weyl group. The key step is to show that the reductive centralizer in $G$ of a minimal nilpotent element has identity component with simply connected derived subgroup and admits no nontrivial algebraic central extensions by $\mathbb G_m$. This gives an isomorphism of based rings between the asymptotic ring of the extended cell and a matrix ring over the representation ring of the centralizer, with matrix size equal to the Euler characteristic of the Springer fiber, namely $|W_0|/2$.

papers.title: On Base Change of Local Stability in Positive Characteristics
papers.abstract:
Let $X\to(C,c)$ be a flat family over a smooth curve germ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, with geometrically integral generic fiber. We show that the fiber pair stays log canonical after every finite dominant base change by a smooth curve if and only if it is log canonical after every finite Frobenius base change, including the original stage.
  More specifically, under iterated Frobenius pullback, a negative log discrepancy of a vertical divisor goes to minus infinity. For any fixed separable cover, however, log canonicity along the Frobenius tower of the original family gives a uniform lower bound instead. Putting these two bounds side by side gives the result for separable covers of arbitrary degree. We also illustrate that the single first Frobenius base change does not suffice in our criterion by an example. Finally, we include two more examples related to the main problem. Neither resolution of singularities nor inversion of adjunction is used.

papers.title: On characters of irreducible modules for Lie superalgebra q(n)
papers.abstract: Su and Zhang proved a formula for the decomposition of characters of irreducible finite dimensional modules over Lie superalgebra $\frak q(n)$ as the sum of Euler characters. They gave a combinatorial formula for the coefficients in that decomposition by generalasing of weights and caps diagrams introduced by J. Brundan and C. Ctroppel. In the present paper we give a correct version of their combinatorial formula. Our main technical tool is a family of creation operators.

papers.title: On dualizability and invertibility in the higher Morita category
papers.abstract:
We prove a conjecture of Lurie characterizing $(n+1)$-dualizability in higher Morita categories of $\mathbb{E}_n$-algebras in terms of dualizability over certain factorization homologies. A key ingredient is a higher Morita category based on the recently developed framework of pointless factorization algebras of Karlsson and the first author. We also verify an invertibility conjecture of Brochier--Jordan--Safranov--Snyder as an immediate corollary of our main result.
  Moreover, we prove a relative version of the dualizability conjecture, yielding a new criterion for relative/twisted field theories. We give some examples, including Dirichlet and Neumann relative theories.

papers.title: On group rings of the simple group of order 168, 504 or 360 and their modules
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be a prime and $\mathbb{Z}_p$ the ring of $p$-adic integers. Let $G$ denote the simple group of order 168, 504 or 360. In this paper, we study the structure of the $\chi$-part of a $\mathbb{Z}_p[\mathrm{Im}(\chi)][G]$-module come from ideal class groups, Artin $L$-functions and Iwasawa theory. After this manuscript was posted, it was pointed out to the author that the main theorem holds for an arbitrary finite group and follows directly from the structure theorem for group rings; see the note added after Theorem 1.1.

papers.title: On irregular threefolds of Kodaira dimension two
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be an irregular threefold of Kodaira dimension two. We show that the Iitaka volume $\operatorname{Ivol}(X)$ of $X$ is at least $\frac{1}{100}$ and $\lvert mK_X\rvert$ defines the Iitaka fibration for $m\geq 32$. Both $\frac{1}{100}$ and $32$ are sharp.

papers.title: On mappings with Jacobian one
papers.abstract: We show that the set $A(n, d)$ of polynomial automorphisms $F : \Bbb C^n \to \Bbb C^n$ of degree at most $d$ and with $Jac(F ) = 1$ is Zariski closed. In particular every irreducible component of the set $A(n,d)$ of polynomial mappings with Jacobian $1$ is either composed with polynomial automorphisms or (generically) with counterexamples to the Jacobian Conjecture. Moreover every such component has dimension at least $n^2-1.$ In particular if the set $X(n,d)$ is irreducible, and $n\ge 3, d\ge 7$, then a generic element of this set is a counterexample to the Jacobian Conjecture.

papers.title: On Perfectoidization of Finite Algebras over a Perfectoid Ring
papers.abstract: We study general properties of the perfectoidization of finite algebras over a perfectoid ring, which helps to understand some precise and explicit descriptions. For example, we prove that if $A=R[t]/(m(t))$ where $m(t)$ is monic, $R$ is perfectoid and the discriminant $d$ of $m(t)$ is a non-zero divisor of $R$ satisfying a bounded torsion condition, then $dA_{\mathrm{pfd}}\subset A$. We also prove a density criterion reducing the construction of the perfectoidization to adjoining suitable $p$-power roots modulo $p$. In the second part of the paper, we compute perfectoidizations in several families of examples, including Kummer-type extensions and split finite algebras.

papers.title: On smooth and bundle structures on topological manifolds homotopy equivalent to $S^{4k-1}$-bundles over $S^{4k}$
papers.abstract: We first verify the expected calculations of the topological structure set, in the sense of surgery theory, for the total spaces of $S^{4k-1}$-bundles over $S^{4k}$ for $k\ge3$, in which manifolds homotopy equivalent to the total spaces are organized. Next, we investigate the question of which of the elements in these structure sets can be realized as such bundles. Moreover, we study the forgetful map from the smooth version to the topological version of the structure set; we determine its image. All elements in the image turn out to have the underlying manifold such a bundle.

papers.title: On Tam's star-shapedness conjecture for numerical ranges of compact adjoint orbits
papers.abstract: We settle Tam's star-shapedness conjecture for numerical ranges associated with compact adjoint orbits of complex reductive Lie algebras, including its original formulation in terms of the inner product $B_\theta$. Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a complex semisimple Lie algebra, and let $K$ be a connected compact Lie group whose Lie algebra is a compact real form of $\mathfrak{g}$. For any $x\in\mathfrak{g}$ and any complex linear functional $f\in\mathfrak{g}^*$, we prove that $\{ f( \operatorname{Ad} (k) x): k \in K \}$ is star-shaped about zero. In the reductive case, the star center is given by the value of $f$ on the central component of $x$, which coincides with the $B_\theta$-pairing of the central components in Tam's original formulation. Our proof is uniform for all complex semisimple Lie algebras. Indeed, using the adjoint Casimir operator, we show that all coordinate functions of the orbit map share a common Laplace eigenvalue; we then use a nodal-hypersurface argument to prove star-shapedness for complex-valued functions in a single eigenspace. The geometric argument relies on a two-sided hypersurface-separation property, which holds whenever the first real cohomology group vanishes. In particular, we do not need simple connectivity or real analyticity. More generally, for finite-dimensional representations of compact connected semisimple Lie groups, we establish star-shapedness whenever the nonfixed component of the orbit vector belongs to a single positive Casimir eigenspace.

papers.title: On the elliptic Hall category
papers.abstract: In this paper we study (the positive half of) the elliptic Hall category, a categorical version of the elliptic Hall algebra. Our main result is a computation of categorical versions of the generators in the coherent realization of the elliptic Hall category, i.e., via coherent sheaves on commuting stacks for $\operatorname{GL}_n\times \mathfrak{gl}_n$: we realize them as Hodge associated graded sheaves of certain twisted equivariant $D$-modules on the groups $\operatorname{GL}_n$.

papers.title: On the Face Map of the Admissible Set With Parahoric Level
papers.abstract: To each face $\mathcal{F}$ of the coweight polytope $\mathcal{P}_{\mu}$, we associate a subset $\text{Adm}(\mu)_{\mathcal{F}}$ of the $\mu$-admissible set $\text{Adm}(\mu)$, which we refer to as a face of $\text{Adm}(\mu)$. This gives rise to a face decomposition of $\text{Adm}(\mu)$. As an application, we give a complete description of the fibers of the face map $|\Delta|^f$ defined by Pappas-Rapoport and prove that the face map is surjective.

papers.title: On the topological invariance of the algebraic multiplicity of holomorphic foliations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we address one of the most basic and fundamental problems in the theory of foliations and ODEs, the topological invariance of the algebraic multiplicity of a holomorphic foliation. For instance, we prove an adapted version of A'Campo-L\^e's Theorem for foliations, i.e., the algebraic multiplicity equal to one is a topological invariant in dimension two. This result is further generalized to higher dimensions under mild conditions; as a consequence, we prove that saddle-nodes are topologically invariant. We prove that the algebraic multiplicity is a topological invariant in several classes of foliations that contain, for instance, the generalized curves and the foliations of second type. Additionally, we address a fundamental result by Rosas-Bazan, which states that the existence of a homeomorphism extending through a neighborhood of the exceptional divisor of the first blow-up implies the topological invariance of the algebraic multiplicity. We show that the result holds if the homeomorphism extends locally near a singularity, even if it does not extend over the entire divisor.

papers.title: On the Torsion Subgroup of the N\'eron--Severi Group
papers.abstract: We prove an explicit bound for the torsion subgroup of the N\'eron--Severi group of a smooth projective complex variety. The proof combines the Diophantine-approximation method of Ziyang Gao and the author (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22285) with Lefschetz fibrations. As an application, we deduce an explicit bound for the torsion sections of a traceless abelian scheme over a complex curve.

papers.title: On the weight zero compactly supported cohomology of $\mathcal{H}_{g, n}$
papers.abstract: For $g\ge 2$ and $n\ge 0$, let $\mathcal{H}_{g,n}\subset \mathcal{M}_{g,n}$ denote the complex moduli stack of $n$-marked smooth hyperelliptic curves of genus $g$. A normal crossings compactification of this space is provided by the theory of pointed admissible $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-covers. We explicitly determine the resulting dual complex, and we use this to define a graph complex which computes the weight zero compactly supported cohomology of $\mathcal{H}_{g, n}$. Using this graph complex, we give a sum-over-graphs formula for the $S_n$-equivariant weight zero compactly supported Euler characteristic of $\mathcal{H}_{g, n}$. This formula allows for the computer-aided calculation, for each $g\le 7$, of the generating function $\mathsf{h}_g$ for these equivariant Euler characteristics for all $n$. More generally, we determine the dual complex of the boundary in any moduli space of pointed admissible $G$-covers of genus zero curves, when $G$ is a cyclic group of prime order, as a symmetric $\Delta$-complex. We use these complexes to generalize our formula for $\mathsf{h}_g$ to moduli spaces of $n$-pointed smooth prime cyclic covers of genus zero curves. This version contains corrections to the published version: see the attached erratum.

papers.title: One ring to rule them all: syzygy maximization for Argyres-Douglas
papers.abstract: We propose a uniform construction of affine schemes encoding the Higgs branches and Macdonald indices of the Argyres--Douglas theories $\mathcal{D}_p(ADE)$, with $\gcd(p,h^\vee)=1$. The construction captures conjectural OPE decoupling relations via the Jacobian ring of a single invariant polynomial potential, obtained from a polynomial twisted period of the corresponding Coxeter orbit space. We show that these potentials are ``syzygy-maximizing'' in the first jet schemes and recover the Higgs branches as their reduced critical loci. We obtain closed determinant expressions for the classical types and explicit potentials for $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$. Powers of the nilradical define an intrinsic filtration on the resulting Jacobian rings, from which we compute candidate Macdonald indices with the correct Schur and Hall--Littlewood limits, in the examples studied. Restricting the potentials to Slodowy slices extends the prescription to nilpotently Higgsed theories. We further conjecture that these Jacobian rings are isomorphic to Zhu's $C_2$-algebras of simple affine VOAs at boundary admissible levels and their quantum Drinfeld--Sokolov reductions.

papers.title: One-cycles on Gushel-Mukai fourfolds and the Beauville-Voisin filtration
papers.abstract: We prove that the invariant locus of the involution associated to a general double EPW sextic is a constant surface and introduce a filtration on $\CH_1$ of a Gushel-Mukai fourfold. We verify the sheaf/cycle correspondence for sheaves supported on low degree rational curves, parallel to the cubic fourfolds case.

papers.title: Open extension of a genus zero Hurwitz-Frobenius manifold
papers.abstract:
Every Dubrovin--Frobenius manifold provides a solution to the WDVV equation, that was initially formulated in the study of the moduli space of curves. During the last two decades special attention was given to the "open" version of the moduli space of curves. Its genus zero intersection theory is governed by the system of equations called open WDVV equation, that extends "classical" WDVV equation.
  In this note we study Dubrovin--Frobenius manifold structures on the Hurwitz spaces of genus zero. We construct explicitly the solutions to open WDVV equation for these Dubrovin--Frobenius manifolds and show that these solutions appear as the restriction of the Dubrovin--Frobenius structure to its discriminant.

papers.title: Parabolic filtrations of Soergel bimodules
papers.abstract: Given a Coxeter system $(W,S)$ and a subset $I\subset S$. Let $W_I=\langle I\rangle$ be the standard parabolic subgroup of a Coxeter group $W$, and ${}^IW$ be the set of representatives of minimal length in the coset $W_I\backslash W$. We construct a parabolic version of Soergel's standard filtration, and show that, given any Soergel bimodule, each subquotient of its parabolic filtration is a direct sum of grading shifts of $B_x^I\otimes_R R_y$ with $x\in W_I$ and $y\in {}^IW$. By applying the character theorem of Elias and Williamson, we deduce the positivity of coefficients in the expansion of $C_w$ with respect to the hybrid basis $\{C_xT_y:x\in W_I,y\in {}^IW\}$. This generalizes Grojnowski and Haiman's result to any Coxeter group.

papers.title: Polynomial parametrizations for two classes of Diophantine equations
papers.abstract: We prove that the integer solution sets of two classes of Diophantine equations are finite unions of polynomial families with integer coefficients and unrestricted integer parameters. In the first class, each monomial, with at most one exception, contains a variable that occurs to the first power and in no other monomial. The second class consists of equations $M=f(t)$, where $M$ is a monomial independent of $t$ with a variable occurring to the first power, and $f\in\Z[t]$ splits completely over $\Q$. If $M$ involves at most two variables, $f$ may instead be an arbitrary quadratic polynomial. We also give complete formulas for five equations listed as open in the monograph \emph{Polynomial Diophantine Equations: A Systematic Approach} (2024).

papers.title: Polynomial Residual Networks are Generically Identifiable
papers.abstract: We prove identifiability results for constant-width residual networks with polynomial activations and bias terms. For activations of degree at least five with generic coefficients, the fiber over a generic parameter is a singleton. For activations of degree at least three with no linear term after a suitable translation of the input, the generic fiber is given by translating biases and then scaling weights and translated biases by real roots of unity. These results specialize to networks without bias terms. With the same proof technique, we further derive necessary conditions for critical points of the ResNet parametrization, that are central in singular learning theory.

papers.title: Polynomiality of Stretched Schubert Structure Constants and Key Coefficients
papers.abstract: We prove that monomial coefficients in affine families of key and Schubert polynomials are eventually polynomial. These results extend to finite products. Using M.~Watanabe's Schubert duality, we deduce that stretched Schubert structure constants are eventually polynomial. This proves a conjecture stated by I.~Pak and Z.~Slonim. We also prove that the positive key expansion of every affine-code family of Schubert polynomials eventually has fixed coefficients and affine indices. The proofs combine Demazure operators and vector partition functions with P.~Magyar's orthodontic formula and the generalized Demazure character theory of V.~Lakshmibai, P.~Littelmann, and P.~Magyar.

papers.title: Positivity of Relative Pluricanonical Direct Images via Fixed-Point Metrics
papers.abstract: We develop a direct analytic approach to positivity of relative pluricanonical direct images through a fixed-point Hermitian metric by direct differential curvature calculations. The curvature resolvent formula from fixed-point equation leads to two-sided estimates of entire Nakano curvature by determinant curvature. In this way, we identify generic rank of determinant curvature with birational variation dimension for a projective algebraic fibration between smooth connected projective varieties with general fiber of general type and maximal birational variation, assuming $mK_F$ is globally generated or the $m$-canonical map is birational for general fiber $F$. In the global generation case, Green--Griffiths Conjecture asks for the tautological bigness of the ordinary symmetric powers $\operatorname{Sym}^{\ell}f_*\omega_{X/Y}^{\otimes m}$, without passing to reflexive hulls, for $\ell\geq P_m(F)=h^0(F,mK_F)$ whenever $m\geq 1$. We prove it for all $\ell\geq1$ at levels $m\geq 2$, also in the case of birational $m$-canonical map, but construct a counterexample at level $m=1$. Over curves, curvature and boundary estimates give a direct analytic proof of Viehweg's ampleness theorem requested by Fujino. For smooth projective families, we also establish numerical dimension and vanishing results related to the birational variation dimension.

papers.title: Prolongation rigidity of sub-free Lie algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that if the 0-th Tanaka prolongation $\mathfrak{g}_0=\mathfrak{der}_0(\mathfrak{m})$ of a fundamental graded nilpotent Lie algebra $\mathfrak{m}=\mathfrak{g}_{-s}\oplus\dots\oplus\mathfrak{g}_{-1}$ is irreducible on $\mathfrak{g}_{-1}$, then $\mathfrak{m}$ is prolongation rigid: $\text{pr}_+(\mathfrak{m})=0$. The only exceptions are given by negative gradations of maximal parabolic subalgebras of a simple Lie algebra.

papers.title: Quasi locally free sheaves on primitive double schemes
papers.abstract: Let $X_2$ be a complex primitive double scheme, $X=(X_2)_{red}$. The ideal sheaf of $X$ is a line bundle on $X$. Let $E$ be a coherent sheaf on $X_2$. Then there exists a nonempty open subset $U$ of $X_2$ and integers $m_1$, $m_2$, uniquely determined by $E$, such that $E_{|U}$ is locally isomorphic to $(O_X\otimes C^{m_1})\oplus(O_{X_2}\otimes C^{m_2})$. If we can take $U=X_2$, we say the $E$ is quasi locally free. If $m_1=1$ we say that $E$ is rigid. In this case, we show that deformations of $E$ are of the same type. So locally free sheaves and rigid quasi locally free sheaves on $X_2$ play the same role on $X_2$ as locally free sheaves do on smooth schemes. In this paper we study the existence and description of quasi locally free sheaves, and flat families of such sheaves.

papers.title: Quasi-canonical lifting of projective varieties in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: The main aim of this article is to give new classes of smooth projective varieties over characteristic $p>0$ that admit flat liftings over the Witt vectors together with additional data (logarithmic structure and the Frobenius morphism) by showing a descending property of such Frobenius liftability. We establish a refined form of the classical result due to Mehta-Srinivas on the existence of canonical liftings. For this purpose, we also establish a result on the algebraization of certain $p$-adic formal schemes.

papers.title: Radical subgroups of finite reductive groups
papers.abstract: Radical subgroups play an important role in both finite group theory and representation theory. This is the first of a series of papers of ours in classifying radical $p$-subgroups of finite reductive groups and in verifying the inductive blockwise Alperin weight condition for them, contributing to the program of proving the Alperin weight conjecture by verifying its inductive condition for finite simple groups. In this paper we present a uniform method for classifying radical subgroups of finite reductive groups. As applications, we investigate the inductive blockwise Alperin weight condition for classical groups, as well as groups of type $F_4$.

papers.title: Range characterization of the cosine transform on higher Grassmannians
papers.abstract: We characterize the range of the cosine transform on real Grassmannians in terms of the decomposition under the action of the special orthogonal group SO(n). Also a geometric interpretation of its image is given. The non- Archimedean analogues are discussed.

papers.title: Rational Cherednik algebras and torus knot Invariants
papers.abstract: The HOMFLY polynomial of the $(m,n)$ torus knot $T_{m,n}$ can be extracted from the doubly graded character of the finite-dimensional representation $L_{m/n}$ of the type $A_{n-1}$ rational Cherednik algebra as observed by Gorsky, Oblomkov, Rasmussen and Shende. It is furthermore conjectured that one can obtain the triply-graded Khovanov-Rozansky homology of $T_{m,n}$ by considering a certain filtration on $L_{m/n}$. In this paper, we show that two of the proposed candidates, the algebraic filtration and the inductive filtration, are equal.

papers.title: Rational limit of Rains integrals of type $A_n$
papers.abstract: We deduce the rational analogue of the elliptic Rains identity of type $A_n$ arXiv:0309252. We also derive reductions of the rational analogue and present the connection of them with well-known integrals in literature.

papers.title: Recovering the Topology of a Real Plane Algebraic Curve by Tropical Homotopy
papers.abstract: We present a tropical homotopy method for computing the numbers of ovals and unbounded components of a real plane algebraic curve, together with the pairing of its ends at infinity. Under explicit support and nondegeneracy assumptions, the homotopy starts from a tropical patchwork and encounters finitely many events. At Morse event points, the curve changes by local surgery. To determine the global attachments, we follow descending separatrices of a single gradient-like field to a fixed collection of base curves. The order of their landing points defines a finite combinatorial state, updated by local rules that also handle events at infinity and simultaneous event points. This recovers component data without tracing the intervening curves. For the dequantizing lifting, given by the negative logarithms of coefficient magnitudes, we prove an explicit event window when the lifting is generic. For fixed support and coefficient signs, with independent, identically distributed log-normal magnitudes, the expected number of events is bounded by a constant divided by the standard deviation of the logarithms. When all event points are Morse, correctness is conditional on complete, correctly classified event data, a sufficiently small starting parameter, and correctly labelled and ordered landing points. A numerical implementation illustrates its behaviour on sparse curves of high degree and on coefficients spanning many scales; these conditions are not certified.

papers.title: Reducibility of linear representations, free ideals, and Kippenhahn's conjecture
papers.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study of the characteristic polynomial of matrix tuples and finite dimensional group representations. Among other things, several key concepts are introduced, including the minimal polynomial, algebraic extension, spectral index and multiplicity, and characteristic graph. Notably, this framework leads to a complete resolution of Kippenhahn's conjecture by providing necessary and sufficient conditions for its validity.

papers.title: Relative delooping levels on intervals of torsion classes
papers.abstract: Let $U$ be a support $\tau$-tilting module over a finite-dimensional algebra $A$, and let $\mathcal{V}\subseteq\operatorname{Fac}U$ be any torsion class. The exact heart $\mathcal{H}=\operatorname{Fac}U\cap\mathcal{V}^{\perp}$ has an Ext-progenerator $P$. We prove that $\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,-)$ realizes $\mathcal{H}$ as a submodule-closed exact subcategory of $\operatorname{mod}B$, where $B=\text{End}_A(P)$, and preserves minimal syzygies. The global relative $k$-delooping levels are independent of $k\geq1$. Writing $g=\operatorname{glo}\text{-}\operatorname{dell}\mathcal{H}$, we obtain the sharp comparison $g\leq\operatorname{glo}\text{-}\operatorname{dell}B\leq g+1$ and $\operatorname{findim}B^{\mathrm{op}}\leq g+1$. Thus the two global levels are finite simultaneously. For wide hearts the relative levels equal their classical counterparts. We also characterize syzygy finiteness of $B$ by a finite relative syzygy stratum and obtain explicit bounds for both finitistic dimensions. If the heart is Frobenius, it is exactly the category of finitely generated Gorenstein-projective $B$-modules under this realization, and both self-injective dimensions of $B$ are at most one. We also give examples to show the main results.

papers.title: Representation theory of the real Gelfand order and real Harish-Chandra modules for $\mathsf{SL}_2(\mathbbm{R})$
papers.abstract: In this article we study the principal block of the category of real Harish-Chandra modules for the group $\mathsf{SL}_2(\RR)$ and relate it to the category of finite dimensional modules over the so-called real Gelfand order. We describe several distinguished classes of the corresponding indecomposable representations.

papers.title: Representation type of contraction algebras
papers.abstract: We classify the representation-finite, tame, and wild contraction algebras arising from 3-fold flopping contractions of isolated cDV singularities with at worst Gorenstein terminal sources. To achieve this, we first determine the representation type of all contracted preprojective algebras of Dynkin types $\mathsf{A}$, $\mathsf{D}$, and $\mathsf{E}$, and then use the representation type invariance under iterated flops and the radical structure of contraction algebras.

papers.title: Representations of generalized linear Reedy categories and abelian model structures
papers.abstract: We study representations of generalized $k$-linear Reedy categories, extending both the linear Reedy categories of Dalezios and \v{S}t'ov\'{\i}\v{c}ek and $k$-linearizations of generalized Reedy categories of Berger and Moerdijk. We establish homological properties of standard modules and classify irreducible representations in terms of simple modules over the local endomorphism algebras. We give criteria for a decomposition of the representation category into a product of local module categories; under the hypotheses of our non-degeneracy criterion, this decomposition holds if and only if the category is Hom-finite over $k$. Applications include span categories and representations of combinatorial categories. Using Grothendieck bifibrations, we then lift families of complete cotorsion pairs on the local module categories to complete cotorsion pairs on the representation category. Under compatibility assumptions, this also lifts families of (hereditary) Hovey triples and yields abelian model structures, with applications to Gorenstein homological algebra.

papers.title: Resolution quivers and the QF-1 property of higher Auslander Nakayama algebras
papers.abstract: We give a resolution-quiver-theoretic proof of the QF-1 conjecture of Cruz and Marczinzik for higher Auslander Nakayama algebras of positive even global dimension. The proof combines syzygy calculations in Kupisch coordinates, which show that the projective dimensions of quotients of a fixed projective module with cyclic top strictly decrease as their lengths increase, with a torsion-pair argument and Morita's criterion.

papers.title: Risk Aversion and Information in Robust Contracting
papers.abstract: We study hidden-action contracting with a risk-averse agent and partial knowledge of actions in a compact convex envelope of distribution--cost pairs. With finitely many outcomes and bounded deterministic wages, the principal's worst-case payoff admits an exact dual representation with an endogenous $f$-divergence governed by transfer utility and an incentive multiplier. Under strictly concave utility, finite-multiplier branch optima follow a truncated likelihood-ratio rule, including at zero-probability outcomes. To address nonattainment induced by adversarial tie-breaking, we characterize the infinite-multiplier limit as a restricted zero-sum game. For polyhedral envelopes, we establish two-sided $O(1/\lambda)$ convergence when inverse utility is Lipschitz. Positive tolerance for suboptimal agent responses restores existence and confines the multiplier search to an explicit compact interval. A finite optimal multiplier gives a linear upper bound on tolerance loss; an optimal infinite-multiplier endpoint in a polyhedral envelope gives a square-root upper bound. A two-action example attains the square-root rate asymptotically. Restricting contracts to a coarse performance statistic contracts the endogenous divergence. We characterize equality in data processing under wage bounds, bracket the value of finer contractible information using fine and coarse dual minimizers, and derive quantitative bounds for approximately sufficient statistics. Numerical experiments demonstrate strict gains over utility-affine contracts and distinguish technological knowledge from the richness of contractible performance signals.

papers.title: Sharp effective Nullstellensatz for projective Cohen-Macaulay schemes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove a sharp effective Nullstellensatz for projective Cohen-Macaulay schemes of pure dimension over an arbitrary field. In particular, if L is an ample line bundle on a smooth complex projective variety X and J is a coherent ideal sheaf with J\otimes L globally generated, then (\sqrt{J})^{\deg_L X}\subseteq J. This establishes the sharp bound conjectured by Ein and Lazarsfeld. More generally, we obtain sharp bounds in terms of mixed intersection numbers and a refinement involving products of powers of prime ideal sheaves associated to the irreducible components of the base locus. We also establish sharp radical power bounds for homogeneous ideals in finitely generated standard graded Cohen-Macaulay domains, extending Koll\'ar's sharp effective Nullstellensatz for polynomial rings. The proofs combine purity and cycle preservation for leading Ext sheaves with Koszul evaluation maps compatible with successive divisor cuts.

papers.title: Sheaves on nodal singularities I
papers.abstract: We study two families of moduli spaces of sheaves attached to the node, namely the punctual Hilbert schemes of the non-reduced plane curve $x^uy^v=0$, and the punctual Quot schemes of the module $k[[x]]^u\oplus k[[y]]^v$ over the reduced node $xy=0$. We compute their motivic generating functions for all $u,v$ and over every field. Both are specializations of a single rational function whose numerator counts matrices by rank, and they are related by the substitution $\mathbb{L}\mapsto Q\mathbb{L}$. This proves the Hilb--Quot correspondence for the node with independent ranks on the two branches. The main geometric ingredient is an elementary modification of an ideal along a branch of the curve, whose fibres are affine spaces of dimension equal to a contact length. We also construct stratifications of the Hilbert schemes into products of affine spaces and tori, and we formulate a branchwise Hilb--Quot--HOMFLY conjecture, which we test on the colored Hopf link.

papers.title: Smale's sixth problem for five bodies in the plane, with a proof formalized in Lean
papers.abstract: We prove that for every choice of five positive masses the planar five-body problem has finitely many central configurations up to similarity. This settles Smale's sixth problem for five bodies in the plane. Albouy and Kaloshin proved it for masses outside a closed algebraic subset of codimension two. We follow their method. Infinitely many central configurations would give an algebraic curve of complex solutions. At the places at infinity of the curve the valuations of the mutual distances must balance. We determine the possible valuation vectors at all positive masses, together with the mass conditions under which each can occur. We treat limits in which four bodies form a cluster of zero potential energy by expanding the potential, which is constant along the curve, at a place. This excludes, at every positive mass, one of the two diagrams in which such clusters occur, and part of the other. The same expansion excludes one further diagram at every positive mass. What remains is an exact analysis, by computer algebra, of the sets of mass conditions that can hold together at positive masses. Exact rational certificates show that the balance fails under each of them, except on a few one-parameter families of masses, which we treat separately. On the rays through $(1,4,4,4,4)$ and $(1,1,4,4,4)$ the certificates do not apply. On the first ray they cannot apply: there the complex equations have a continuum of solutions, as Albouy and Kaloshin observed. On these rays we count the real central configurations: there are 306 and 294 up to orientation-preserving similarity. The certificates, the programs that check them and a proof of the theorem in the Lean proof assistant are available.

papers.title: Solvability and nilpotence of ind-groups via tangent curves
papers.abstract: Answering a question of Kraft and the second-named author, we prove that a connected ind-group over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero is solvable, respectively nilpotent, if and only if its Lie algebra is. Their derived lengths, respectively nilpotency classes, coincide. We also obtain bounds on the derived length and nilpotency class for regular linear representations of connected ind-groups and for subgroups generated by connected algebraic subgroups. As an application, we give a new proof of the geometric case of a theorem of Belabbas: a solvable Lie algebra of vector fields on an affine variety generated by finitely many locally finite Lie subalgebras is locally finite and finite dimensional.

papers.title: Some arithmetical aspects of the two dimensional Jacobian Conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove that any counter-example to the two dimensional Jacobian Conjecture with integral coefficients and determinant of its Jacobian matrix equals one, has only paths of asymptotic values that can contain only finitely many points of the planar integral lattice. The second part of our paper gives some nontrivial applications of the theory of certain Theta functions to the two dimensional Jacobian Conjecture over the real field, and over the complex field.

papers.title: Stability functions inducing stability data
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study when a stability data on an abelian length category is induced by a stability function. We give an intrinsic characterization of such stability data. For at most six phases, an inducing function exists if and only if every semistable subcategory is wide. An example with seven phases shows that this bound is sharp. For finite phase sets and finite rank, an inducing function exists if and only if an inducing red path exists. We also give a maximal green sequence of length eleven in type $D_4$ that no stability function induces. This disproves the red-path conjecture of Br\"ustle--Smith--Treffinger.

papers.title: Stability of certain elements in the Bernstein center
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a split connected reductive algebraic group over a non-archimedean local field $F$ of characteristic zero. The stable center conjecture asserts that the subspace of stable elements in the Bernstein center of $G(F)$ is a sub-algebra, and this subring is conjecturally isomorphic to the regular functions on the moduli of semi-simple Langlands parameters. Bezrukavnikov-Kazhdan-Varshavsky suggested an approach towards the stable center conjecture by explicitly constructing elements and proving their stability directly without assuming LLC, and proved the stability of the depth-$r$ projectors. Following the idea, the first author and Tsao-Hsien Chen produced a family of elements in the center which are conjecturally stable using Deligne-Lusztig parameters attached to irreducible representations. This paper proves the stability of the projectors corresponding to strongly regular Deligne-Lusztig parameters in depth-zero, and for all the positive depth elements with some restrictions on the residue characteristic.

papers.title: Structural taxonomy and complex irreducible representations of non-abelian groups of order p^4
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $G$ be a non-abelian group of order $p^4$. The classification of groups of order $p^4$ provides a natural setting for studying the structure of their complex group algebras. In this paper, we consider a non-abelian group G of order $p^4$ and determine the primitive central idempotents of the complex group algebra $\mathbb{C}G$. Using these idempotents, we obtain the corresponding decomposition of $\mathbb{C}G$ into simple components and describe the irreducible representations of $G$. The results provide an explicit description of the representation-theoretic structure of the chosen non-abelian group of order $p^4$ and illustrate the role of primitive central idempotents in the Wedderburn decomposition of its complex group algebra.

papers.title: Symbolic Integration of Differential Forms: From Abel to Zeilberger
papers.abstract: This paper focuses on symbolic integration of differential forms, with a particular emphasis on historical and modern developments, from Abel's addition theorems for Abelian integrals to Zeilberger's creative telescoping for parameterized integrals. It explores closed rational $p$-forms and provides algorithmic approaches for their integration, extending classical results like Hermite reduction and Liouville's theorem. The integration of closed differential forms with parameters is further examined through telescopers, offering a unified framework for handling both algebraic and transcendental cases.

papers.title: Symplectic singularity as hyperK\"ahler cone
papers.abstract: We prove that any symplectic singularity has a structure of hyperK\"ahler cone. In particular, it is equivalent to the vertex of a conical symplectic variety, and it is automatically K-polystable.

papers.title: Synthetic geometry of differential equations: I. Jets and comonad structure
papers.abstract: We give an abstract formulation of the formal theory partial differential equations (PDEs) in synthetic differential geometry, one that would seamlessly generalize the traditional theory to a range of enhanced contexts, such as super-geometry, higher (stacky) differential geometry, or even a combination of both. A motivation for such a level of generality is the eventual goal of solving the open problem of covariant geometric pre-quantization of locally variational field theories, which may include fermions and (higher) gauge fields. (abridged)

papers.title: The $\rho$-Fourier transform
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a reductive group over a local field $F$ and let $\rho:{}^LG \to \mathrm{GL}_{V_{\rho}}(\mathbb{C})$ be a representation of its $L$-group satisfying suitable assumptions. Braverman, Kazhdan and Ng\^o conjectured that one has a $\rho$-Fourier transform satisfying certain desiderata. We give a uniform construction of the Fourier transform for arbitrary local fields. This complements work of L.~Lafforgue in the non-Archimedean case, and proves a portion of the conjectures of Braverman, Kazhdan and Ng\^o. Our methods are spectral in nature.

papers.title: The algebraic K-theory of $k[\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)]$
papers.abstract: We compute via trace methods the higher algebraic $K$-theory of the group ring $k[\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)]$, as well as the related groups $\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$, $\operatorname{PGL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$, and $\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$, where $k$ is a finite field of characteristic $p$ and $q=p^r$. At the core of the computation is the algebraic $K$-theory of the group ring of the Sylow $p$-subgroup, $k[C_p^r]$, which we determine via a theorem of L\"uck--Reich--Rognes--Varisco on cyclic assembly for topological cyclic homology. In the process, we reprove the cyclic assembly result in the language of Nikolaus--Scholze, analyse assembly for smaller families of subgroups, and develop further tools for computing topological cyclic homology of group rings.

papers.title: The Brauer $A(\infty)$ condition and Navarro's conjecture on Brauer characters under coprime actions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove the Brauer $A(\infty)$ condition for good non-defining primes. Consequently, we show a conjecture of Navarro on coprime actions and Brauer characters for primes larger than 3.

papers.title: The fundamental theorem of tropical differential algebra for formal Puiseux series
papers.abstract: The fundamental theorem of tropical differential algebra has been established for formal power series solutions of systems of algebraic differential equations. It has been shown that the direct extension to formal Puiseux series solutions fails. In this paper, we overcome this issue by transforming the given differential system and such a generalization is presented. Moreover, we explain why such transformations do not work for generalizing the fundamental theorem to transseries solutions, and show that one inclusion still holds for this case even without using any transformation.

papers.title: The generalized Dixmier conjecture and the two-dimensional Jacobian conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove that the two-dimensional Jacobian conjecture $\mathrm{JC}_2$ implies the generalized Dixmier conjecture $\mathrm{DC}'_1$ for the first Weyl algebra $A_1$, which states, in one of several equivalent formulations, that every endomorphism of the two-by-two matrix ring $\operatorname{Mat}_2(A_1)$ is invertible. For the converse, an endomorphism of $\mathbb A^2_{\mathbb C}$ with Jacobian one gives rise to a family of holonomic $A_2$-modules over finite fields. One needs to lift this family to an $A_2$-module in characteristic zero with the prescribed arithmetic support. The existence of such a lift is a special case of Kontsevich's conjecture on holonomic $\mathcal D$-modules with prescribed arithmetic support. We prove that in this special situation such a lift is unique whenever it exists. If these lifts exists for every endomorphism with Jacobian one, then $\mathrm{DC}'_1$ implies $\mathrm{JC}_2$. For every $n\ge 3$, we construct a Lagrangian subvariety of $T^*\mathbb{A}^n$ that provides a counterexample to Kontsevich's conjecture. The counterexamples arise from the graph of a noninvertible symplectic endomorphism of $\mathbb A^4$ constructed by Long. We also present a different strategy for lifting $\mathcal D$-modules associated with a Jacobian-one endomorphism of $\mathbb A^2_{\mathbb C}$ to characteristic zero via ultraproducts and show that the existence of a characteristic-zero lift in this setting is equivalent to the uniform boundedness of the Berest--Wilson invariants of these $A_2$-modules, regarded as left $A_1$-modules. Finally, we study two other conjectures of Kontsevich on arithmetic support, giving a counterexample to one and partial results on the other.

papers.title: The Lichtenbaum-Quillen dimension of complex varieties
papers.abstract: The Lichtenbaum-Quillen conjecture for smooth complex varieties states that algebraic and topological K-theory with finite coefficients become isomorphic in high degrees. We define the "Lichtenbaum-Quillen dimension" of a variety in terms of the point where this happens, show that it is surprisingly computable, and analyze many examples. It gives an obstruction to rationality, but one that turns out to be weaker than unramified cohomology and some related birational invariants defined by Colliot-Th\'el\`ene and Voisin using Bloch-Ogus theory. Because it is compatible with semi-orthogonal decompositions, however, it allows us to prove some new cases of the integral Hodge conjecture using homological projective duality, and to compute the higher algebraic K-theory of the Kuznetsov components of the derived categories of some Fano varieties.

papers.title: The many faces of a logarithmic scheme
papers.abstract: A standard assumption in the study of logarithmic structures is "fineness", but this assumption is not preserved by intersections, fiber products, and more general limits. We explain how a coherent logarithmic scheme $X$ has a natural decomposition into "fine faces" -- a collection of fine logarithmic subschemes. This allows for importation of the techniques of tropical geometry into the study of more general logarithmic schemes. We explain the relevance of the construction in enumerative geometry and moduli via a range of examples. Techniques developed in the study of binomial schemes lead to effective algorithms for computing the fine faces.

papers.title: The modular characters of $\text{Sp}_{10}(2)$
papers.abstract: Using computational methods, we determine the irreducible $3$- and $5$-modular characters of the symplectic group $\text{Sp}_{10}(2)$ for blocks with non cyclic defect groups, with one ambiguity in the principal $3$-block.

papers.title: The operator Hilbert space $\mathrm{OH}$ embeds completely isometrically into a noncommutative $\mathrm{L}^1$-space
papers.abstract: We prove that Pisier's operator Hilbert space $\mathrm{OH}$ embeds completely isometrically into the predual of a $\mathrm{QWEP}$ von Neumann algebra, answering a longstanding question introduced by Pisier and later by Haagerup and Musat. The embedding is obtained as an ultraproduct of free probabilistic models $h_k = \Lambda^{\frac{1}{2}}c_k\Lambda^{\frac{1}{2}}$ realized in the free group factor $\mathrm{VN}(\mathbb{F}_\infty)$, with the trace and circular family scaled according to the mass of the truncated measure $t^{-\frac{5}{3}} \mathrm{d} t$.

papers.title: The regular pentagonal system and the Smith--Ward problem
papers.abstract: The three-dimensional function system of the regular pentagon fails the lifting property, giving a counterexample to the operator-system formulation of the Smith--Ward problem with C$^*$-envelope $\mathbb C^5$. We construct unital $k$-positive maps from this fixed system into matrix algebras where distance from every ucp map is bounded below independently of $k$. We also prove that every regular polygon system with at least five vertices detects nuclearity, while its dual characterizes the weak expectation property. These tensor-product characterizations follow from a graph dichotomy: a graph operator system and its dual are C$^*$-nuclear when the graph is $2$-chordal; otherwise they detect nuclearity and WEP, respectively.

papers.title: The Serre closure of Banach spaces
papers.abstract:
We determine the Serre closure of Banach spaces in the category of quasi-Banach spaces, that is, the smallest class of quasi-Banach spaces that contains all Banach spaces and is stable under subspaces, quotients, and extensions. Precisely, a quasi-Banach space $X$ belongs to this closure if and only if there exist constants $M$ and $k\in\mathbb N$ such that $$ \frac{\|x_1+\dots+x_n\|}{\|x_1\|+\dots+\|x_n\|}\leq M\log^k n $$ for every $n\geq 2$ and every $x_1,\dots,x_n\in X$; equivalently, $X$ is a quotient of an Orlicz sequence space $\ell(I,f_l)$, where $I$ is an index set and $f_l(t)$ is equivalent to $t\log^l(1/t)$ near zero.
  The proof combines geometrical estimates for quasi-Banach spaces and quasilinear maps with the study of higher order derived spaces associated to complex interpolation between $\ell_{2/3}$ and $\ell_2$. We provide examples of spaces in the Serre closure of Banach spaces that are not iterated extensions of Banach spaces and discuss some related problems.

papers.title: The solvable degree of a Schur algebra
papers.abstract:
The solvable degree
  of a Schur algebra $D$ is the greatest common divisor of
  all integers $n$ such that $D^{n\times n}$ is a direct summand of the rational
  group algebra $\Q G$ for some finite solvable group $G$.
  The main result of this paper gives divisibility conditions on the solvable
  degree depending on the center and the rational primes that divide the
  discriminant of $D$.

papers.title: The Unbalanced Group Theorem
papers.abstract: The classification of finite simple groups (CFSG) identifies the basic building blocks of all finite groups. It grew from nineteenth-century work of Galois and Jordan into a collective effort involving many mathematicians, with Gorenstein playing a central organizing role. Its proof is a vast network of interdependent results such as the Feit--Thompson odd-order theorem, the signalizer functor theorem, and Aschbacher's classical involution theorem. The original papers make up the first-generation proof. The second-generation treatment, initiated by Gorenstein, Lyons, and Solomon, reorganizes and simplifies much of this work. A key structural result in the first-generation program is the Unbalanced Group Theorem (UGT). Under the inductive hypotheses of the classification, it says that a nontrivial subgroup of odd order normal in the centralizer of an involution forces the ambient simple group to be a group of Lie type in odd characteristic or one of the alternating groups of certain degrees. While formalizing the first-generation proof, we found counterexamples to a closure assertion used in a published route to UGT. This obstruction concerns that particular argument. UGT also has other proofs. Here we explain the obstruction and develop an alternative argument for the simple-group case using Solomon's 1976 theory of maximal $2$-components, which provides a framework for comparing the simple pieces arising in different involution centralizers.

papers.title: Twisted Yangians of split types BI, CI, DI and Drinfeld type current relations
papers.abstract: We study twisted Yangians associated with the split symmetric pairs of types BI, CI and DI. We introduce a new presentation of these algebras, which we call the transposed presentation, governed by a twisted reflection equation that interacts naturally with the Gaussian decomposition of the generating matrix. Working entirely within the $R$-matrix presentation, we derive Drinfeld-type current presentations of the special twisted Yangian $SY^{\mathrm{tw}}(\mathfrak{g}_N)$ and of the extended twisted Yangian $X^{\mathrm{tw}}(\mathfrak{g}_N)$, in which the Serre relations are stated in a closed current form. Extracting coefficients recovers the Drinfeld presentation of Lu, Wang and Zhang, in the normalisation of Lu. As a consequence, we establish an explicit isomorphism between the $R$-matrix and Drinfeld presentations conjectured by Lu, Wang and Zhang. As a byproduct, we obtain a tensor product decomposition of $X^{\mathrm{tw}}(\mathfrak{g}_N)$ into the twisted Yangian in the Drinfeld presentation and a polynomial ring in countably many central variables. We also obtain Poincar\'e-Birkhoff-Witt bases in the Drinfeld generators and the coideal coproduct on the low Drinfeld modes at all but the last node.

papers.title: Uniform asymptotics and the Weil--Petersson constant
papers.abstract: In their celebrated work on the large-genus asymptotic expansion of Weil--Petersson volumes, Mirzakhani and Zograf left open the question of whether the Weil--Petersson constant satisfies $C_{\mathrm{WP}}=\pi^{-1/2}$. We resolve the conjecture affirmatively. Our strategy is to consider a family of spectral curves interpolating between $y=z-4z^3$ and $y=\sin(2\pi z)/(2\pi)$. For each fixed number $n\geq2$ of marked points, we normalize the cusp coefficients using the action integral and the derivative at its first positive zero. We prove that the logarithmic derivatives of these normalized coefficients with respect to the family parameter are $O_n(g^{-1})$, uniformly along the family. The proof combines the descendant recursion, positivity, the dilaton equation, KdV, and coefficient asymptotics for the Painlev\'e I equation.

papers.title: Uniform large-genus asymptotics of Weil-Petersson volumes
papers.abstract: Let $V_{g,n}$ denote the Weil--Petersson volume of the moduli space of genus-$g$ hyperbolic surfaces with $n$ cusps. We obtain an asymptotic expansion in inverse powers of the genus as $g\to\infty$, uniformly for all $n\ge0$. This includes cusp counts of order $\sqrt g$ and larger, where the fixed-$n$ expansion of Mirzakhani and Zograf no longer gives a uniform approximation. The leading term is explicit and has relative error $O(g^{-1})$. Truncating the expansion at a suitably chosen order proportional to $\sqrt g$ gives relative error $O(\exp(-a\sqrt g))$ for some $a>0$, with no restriction on the growth of $n$. For fixed $n$, the leading term identifies the universal constant in the Mirzakhani--Zograf asymptotics as $1/\sqrt\pi$, as conjectured by Zograf. We also answer two questions of Mirzakhani: we determine explicit asymptotic profiles for volume ratios uniformly in the number of cusps, and for adjacent coefficient ratios of the one-boundary volume polynomial uniformly over all degrees. The proof uses a positive recursion for mixed $\kappa_1$--$\psi$ intersection numbers, with the absolute normalization determined by comparison with the known asymptotics of pure $\psi$ intersection numbers.

papers.title: Unique direct-sum decompositions of infinite-dimensional unitary representations of the infinite dihedral group via real CMV matrices
papers.abstract:
Unitary representations of the infinite dihedral group arise naturally and play an important role in a wide range of areas including mathematics, physics, and engineering. CMV matrices, introduced by Cantero, Moral, and Vel\'azquez, are five-diagonal unitary matrices that are standard tools in the theory of orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle. It is known that every unitary representation of the infinite dihedral group on a separable Hilbert space admits a discrete direct-sum decomposition into representations arising from the natural factorizations of real CMV matrices and copies of two exceptional one-dimensional irreducible representations.
  We prove that such a decomposition is unique up to unitary equivalence when the summands arising from real CMV matrices are grouped according to their multiplicities and the spectral measures of the corresponding matrices are mutually singular across distinct multiplicities. Furthermore, we show that the representation associated with each such real CMV matrix $C$ admits a direct integral decomposition into irreducible unitary representations with respect to the push-forward of the restriction of the spectral measure of $C$ to the closed upper half circle.
  These results make it possible to study the structure of unitary representations of the infinite dihedral group using CMV matrices and the theory of orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle.

papers.title: Uniqueness of four-body convex central configurations for all masses
papers.abstract: We prove that for every choice of four positive masses and every cyclic ordering of the bodies there is exactly one strictly convex planar central configuration with that ordering, up to similarity. This answers Problem 10 in the list of Albouy, Cabral and Santos, which Santoprete calls the Simó--Yoccoz conjecture. The main step is a uniform lower bound for the Hessian at convex central configurations: it is at least one quarter of its radial part, which vanishes only on translations and rotations. Dziobek's relations turn the indefinite part of the Hessian into a negative multiple of a square, and a Cauchy--Schwarz argument bounds this term by the radial part times the trace of an explicit $2\times2$ matrix in which the masses do not appear. We prove that this trace is less than $\frac34$ by interval arithmetic on the three-dimensional set of normalized convex central configurations, in the coordinates of Corbera, Cors and Roberts. Uniqueness then follows by a covering argument from the case of four equal masses. The computation has been repeated with a second, independently written program. The Hessian bound and the uniqueness theorem, including the computation, have been formalized in the Lean proof assistant and checked by its kernel, using only the standard axioms. As consequences, every degenerate four-body central configuration is concave, the convex central configuration depends analytically on the masses, and the known symmetry theorems for kites, isosceles trapezoids and rhombi follow in a few lines. The analytic dependence and the symmetry theorems are also formalized.

papers.title: Uniqueness of the maximal function field with the third largest genus in characteristic $3$
papers.abstract: Let $n$ be a positive integer and define $q=3^n$. It is well known that there exists a maximal function field $Z_3$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ of genus $g_3=q(q-1)/6$ and that $g_3$ is the third largest genus a maximal function field over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ can have. In this article we show that any maximal function field over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ of genus $g_3$ is isomorphic to $Z_3$. This extends previously known uniqueness result for the largest and second largest genera of maximal curves.

papers.title: Universal polynomials for Gromov-Witten invariants on toric surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the polynomiality of combined logarithmic and ordinary Gromov-Witten invariants with a Lambda class insertion on toric surfaces $\Delta(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{d})$. We show that the combined logarithmic Gromov-Witten invariants can be expressed in terms of universal relative node polynomials when the direction vector $\mathbf{c}$ and length vector $\mathbf{d}$ of the $h$-transverse lattice polygon $\Delta(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{d})$ are sufficiently large and spread out. In particular, when the normal fan of the $h$-transverse lattice polygon $\Delta(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{d})$ is smooth and its edges satisfy a length condition, we show that the combined Gromov-Witten invariants are equal to a universal node polynomial. We also show that the higher genus Block-G\"ottsche polynomials of smooth toric surfaces corresponding to these $h$-transverse lattice polygons, including toric blowups beyond Hirzebruch and toric del Pezzo surfaces, are equal to a generating function of higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants.

papers.title: Volume Computation and Comparison for Four-Dimensional Bodies of Constant Width
papers.abstract: We compute and compare the volumes of explicit four-dimensional bodies of constant width one. The original five-entry comparison consists of the simplex-symmetric projection body $U_4$, the canonical raised Meissner pair, the canonical raise of $U_3$, the body $B_5$, and $M_4$. We combine exact geometric formulas, numerical integration, interval enclosures and inscribed rational polytopes to obtain a certified strict ordering of their volumes. We also compare $U_4$ with the direct four-dimensional AMO peabody. The two raised Meissner bodies are proved noncongruent but exactly equal in volume. An introductory account explains why different constructions benefit from different computational methods, and distinguishes approximate volume estimates from inequalities certified by exact or outward-rounded arithmetic.

papers.title: Wehrl-type entropy problem for compact connected semisimple Lie groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a compact connected semisimple Lie group, and let $\pi:G\to U(V_\lambda)$ be a finite-dimensional irreducible unitary representation associated with the highest weight $\lambda$. We prove that coherent projectors are the unique minimizers of the Wehrl entropy over all density matrices on $V_\lambda$. Similar extremal properties hold for power functions in place of the entropy function. The proof uses a second variation at the extremizer by perturbation in directions associated with Killing fields, similar to the strategy of Frank and Lieb used in \cite{FrankLieb}. Then the problem reduces to the uncertainty principle characterizing coherent states. This solves the Wehrl-type entropy problem for arbitrary compact connected semisimple Lie groups.

papers.title: Which Schubert varieties are local complete intersections?
papers.abstract: We characterize by pattern avoidance the Schubert varieties for GL_n which are local complete intersections (lci). For those Schubert varieties which are local complete intersections, we give an explicit minimal set of equations cutting out their neighborhoods at the identity. Although the statement of our characterization only requires ordinary pattern avoidance, showing that the Schubert varieties not satisfying our conditions are not lci appears to require more general notions of pattern avoidance. The Schubert varieties defined by inclusions, originally introduced by Gasharov and Reiner, turn out to be an important subclass, and we further develop some of their combinatorics. Applications include formulas for Kostant polynomials and presentations of cohomology rings for lci Schubert varieties.
